statements.statement_text: The base of a silo must extend beyond any walls of the silo.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record the type and amount of livestock manure.

An application for a derogation must be submitted between 1 October and 31 December in the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates, except that an application relating to the calendar year commencing 1 January 2017 may be submitted by 20 March 2017.
The permitted amount of nitrogen for beetroot, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, calabrese, cauliflower, and leeks (individually or in combination) is 370 kg per hectare (no standard yield applies).
SEPA shall withdraw, extend, or modify a notice under regulation 8(5) if directed to do so by the Scottish Ministers under regulation 9(5).
Fuel oil storage areas must comply with the requirements set out in Schedule 3.
An occupier of a holding who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must produce a plan for the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser for that growing season.
The Secretary of State must make adequate arrangements to enable the public to prepare and participate effectively in the review.
The walls of any pipes associated with slurry or effluent storage must be impermeable.

For each area planted or intended to be planted, the nutrient management plan must record the soil nitrogen supply calculated in accordance with regulation 6(1) and the method used to establish that figure.

The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010, regulations 3 and 9, are revoked in relation to all other holdings (not situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone) on 1 April 2021.
Where paragraph (4)(b) applies, storage facilities for an additional one week's manure must be provided as a contingency measure in the event that spreading is not possible on some dates.
The occupier must record the total agricultural area and the area of grass within the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.
A silo must either comply with the provisions of Schedule 1, or be designed and constructed in accordance with BS 5502 (parts relating to Cylindrical Forage Towers).
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not stored on agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.

A land manager must ensure that reasonable precautions are taken to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from land management and cultivation practices on agricultural land, including practices such as creating farm tracks, establishing seedbeds, polytunnels or tramlines, cleaning out ditches, installing drainage or irrigation, and irrigating or spraying crops.

Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow out of the channel is controlled by a sluice, the capacity of the reception pit must be adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
For livestock manure spread on and after 1 January 2014, the available nitrogen percentages are: cattle slurry 40%, pig slurry 50%, poultry manure 30%, and other livestock manure 10%.

Before 30th April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record for the previous storage period the number of animals in a building or hardstanding on the holding during that period and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1.
Where precision spreading equipment is used, a land manager must ensure that organic manure is not applied within 6 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.

In calculating the area of a holding for the purpose of ascertaining the amount of nitrogen permitted to be spread, no account is to be taken of any land which is covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the year concerned.
In a holding or part of a holding not previously situated within a nitrate vulnerable zone, regulations 17 to 21, 25, 26, and 28 to 31 do not apply until 1 August 2024.
The amount of nitrogen produced by livestock must be calculated in accordance with Schedule 1.

Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record, for the previous storage period referred to in regulation 29, the number and category of animals in a building or on a hardstanding during that storage period.
An occupier who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must first undertake a field inspection to consider the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be located within the bund.
Regulation 22 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser in a greenhouse.
The Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008 are revoked.

A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure the silage is kept in a silo satisfying the requirements of Schedule 1, or compressed into bales that are wrapped/sealed in impermeable membranes or enclosed in impermeable bags and stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter.

The record-keeping obligations in paragraphs (1) and (2) do not apply to the occupier of a holding in any calendar year in which: 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass; the total nitrogen in organic manure applied is no more than 100 kg per hectare; the total nitrogen in manufactured nitrogen fertiliser applied is no more than 90 kg per hectare; and the occupier does not bring any organic manure onto the holding.
A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.
Regulation 4(1) does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker that is used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier must record the amount required and the planned date for spreading (month).
Where any grass on the holding is ploughed, the land must be sown with a crop with high nitrogen demand within four weeks beginning with the day after the ploughing.

Having carried out a review, the Secretary of State must set out the conclusions in a report and publish the report; the report must set out the objectives intended to be achieved by these Regulations, include an assessment of the extent to which those objectives are being achieved, and include an assessment of whether those objectives remain appropriate and, if so, the extent to which they could be achieved in a less burdensome way.

Spreading equipment with a trajectory of more than 4 metres from the ground may be used on land with a low run-off risk where such equipment can achieve an average slurry application rate of not more than 2 mm per hour when operating continuously.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record: (a) the area on which the organic manure will be spread; (b) the quantity of organic manure to be spread; (c) the planned date for spreading (month); (d) the type of organic manure; (e) the total nitrogen content; and (f) the amount of nitrogen likely to be available from the organic manure intended to be spread for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
NRW may at any time extend the period for compliance with any requirement of the notice.

The fertilisation plan must record the amount of nitrogen likely to be available for crop uptake from any organic manure intended to be spread for crop uptake in the growing season during the calendar year in which it is spread, and the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied to meet crop requirement from any organic manure spread or intended to be spread during the calendar year.
The Agency has the function of enforcing the Regulations.

A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land takes into account the weather conditions and forecasts for that land at the time of the application.

Each sample must be poured into a larger container, stirred thoroughly, and a two-litre sample taken from that container and poured into a smaller, clean container; the two-litre sample must then be sent for analysis.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be arranged to discharge vertically downwards.

Before revising or adding to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones, the Secretary of State must publish the proposals and send written notice to any person appearing to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.
For the purposes of paragraph (5), the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure is to be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14.

The accounts must record the weight in tonnes and nitrogen content of all manufactured nitrogen fertiliser stocks held on the holding between 1st January and 31st December, and of all manufactured nitrogen fertiliser brought onto or sent off the holding between those dates.

In calculating the area of a holding for the purpose of ascertaining the amount of nitrogen permitted to be spread, no account is to be taken of any surface waters, hardstanding, buildings, roads or woodland (unless the woodland is used for grazing).
A report under regulation 40(2)(a) must include an assessment of the extent to which the objectives of these Regulations are being achieved.
For permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the regulation 6(1) obligations each year beginning 1 January before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.

The fertilisation plan must record the amount of manufactured nitrogen fertiliser required (being the optimum nitrogen required by the crop less nitrogen available from organic manure spread during that calendar year) and the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser required (being the optimum phosphate required by the crop less phosphate supplied from organic manure spread for fertilising the crop during that calendar year).
Any temporary grassland on sandy soils on the holding must not be ploughed between 1 July and the following 31 December.
A review carried out under regulation 16 must, so far as is reasonable, have regard to how Article 11(3)(h) of Directive 2000/60/EC is implemented in other member States.

The occupier must ensure that the total amount of phosphate from manufactured phosphate fertiliser and phosphate from organic manure spread in the growing season does not, during the relevant period, exceed the limits set out in paragraph 9, irrespective of the figure recorded in the enhanced nutrient management plan under paragraph 7(2)(b).
A temporary field site must not be located in the same place as an earlier temporary field site constructed within the last two years.

A person who applies organic manure onto the surface of bare soil or stubble (other than soil that has been sown) must ensure that the organic manure is incorporated into the soil in accordance with regulation 19.

A person who has custody or control of field silage or silage stored on open land must ensure the place is at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters, and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage effluent could enter if it escaped.

A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain the map published under regulation 3(2), accompanied by a statement detailing the nature of, and reasons for, any revisions to the designated nitrate vulnerable zone since the end of the previous reporting period.
These Regulations are titled the Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021.

The Welsh Ministers must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of the measures imposed by these Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution from agricultural sources.
The slurry or other manure must, if reasonably practicable, be thoroughly mixed before samples are taken, and each sample must be taken from a different location.
The risk map must be completed by 31 March 2024.
A person guilty of an offence under regulation 41 is liable on summary conviction to a fine.
During the relevant period, the spreading of slurry on a holding is subject to specific requirements under Schedule 1A.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record: (a) the area on which the manure is to be spread; (b) the quantity to be spread; (c) the month in which it is to be spread; (d) the type of manure; (e) its total nitrogen content; and (f) the amount of nitrogen likely to be available from the manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.

Where the objectives remain appropriate, a report published under regulation 16 must assess the extent to which those objectives could be achieved in another way which involves less onerous regulatory provision.
The occupier of a holding must record how any grassland was managed in the previous calendar year, before 30 April each year.
Regulation 32 does not apply to crops in a greenhouse.
Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must record the planned month for spreading.
The written declaration must be sent to the Agency within 28 calendar days of the derogation being granted.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not stored on agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the fertilisation plan duty each calendar year before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the total nitrogen content of the manure.
The walls of any pipes associated with slurry or effluent storage must be impermeable.

Any reference in regulation 7(1) to the period stated in a notice means that period as extended if extended under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5) or (6), and any reference to a requirement of a notice means that requirement as modified if modified under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5).

No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in a fuel storage tank or container within a storage area in relation to which the requirements of Schedule 3 are satisfied.

The occupier of a holding, acting on the written advice of a FACTS adviser, may spread or permit the spreading of nitrogen in an amount so advised even if it exceeds the amount that would otherwise be permitted for grass under regulation 12.

statements.statement_text: NRW may at any time modify the requirements of the notice, provided the person on whom the notice is served consents.
Any person who applies organic manure onto the surface of bare soil or stubble (other than soil that has been sown) must ensure that it is incorporated into the soil in accordance with regulation 16.
The occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure for the purposes of regulation 8 by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3.

The occupier must determine the soil phosphorus index for each area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type by using the results from the soil sampling analysis under paragraph 4 and the values in Table 1.
A person must not spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water, except as permitted by regulation 17(2) or 17(4).

A person required to make a record under these Regulations must keep that record for a period of 5 years after the record ceased to be current, regardless of whether the land has since ceased to be designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be arranged to discharge vertically downwards.

"Derogation" means a derogation granted under this Part from the limit on the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure that can be applied to land each year in accordance with paragraph 2(b) of Annex III to Council Directive 91/676/EEC.
No person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on tillage land during the period from 1 September to 15 January (inclusive).
On summary conviction for an offence under regulation 11, a person is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or a fine not exceeding £20,000, or both.

When planning the application of agricultural diffuse pollution sources, the land manager must ensure that the proximity of the land to inland freshwaters, coastal waters, wetlands, or to a spring, well or borehole is taken into account as a factor indicating significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
The occupier must, before spreading organic manure, record the quantity of organic manure to be spread.
A temporary field site must not be located within 30 metres of a watercourse on land identified on the risk map as having an incline of greater than 12°.
For cattle slurry, the available nitrogen for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread is 40% (applicable on and after 1st January 2014).

Where a storage area contains only one fuel storage tank and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of that tank.
Every part of any fuel storage tank must be situated within the bund.
In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duties under paragraph 3(1) in each calendar year before spreading phosphate fertiliser.

The only grounds of appeal under regulation 6 are that the relevant holding (or any part of it) does not drain into water which the Secretary of State proposes to identify (or continue to identify) as polluted, or (in a regulation 5(3A) case) does not drain into water already identified as polluted, or drains into water which the Secretary of State should not identify (or continue to identify) as polluted.
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base shall be provided with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any slurry which may escape from the tank.

As part of the review under regulation 39, the Secretary of State must review the overall position of derogations granted under this regulation against objective criteria including the existence, in designated nitrate vulnerable zones, of long growing seasons, crops with high nitrogen uptake, and soils with exceptionally high denitrification capacity.

The occupier of a relevant holding must, when separating slurry on the holding into its solid and liquid fractions, do so mechanically or on an impermeable surface where the liquid drains into a suitable receptacle.
Separation of slurry into its solid and liquid fractions must either be carried out mechanically or on an impermeable surface where the liquid fraction drains into a suitable receptacle.

Topsoil must not be removed from the ground upon which a temporary field site is to be constructed, and a temporary field site must not be located within 30 metres of a watercourse on land identified on the risk map as having an incline of greater than 12°.
On determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers may dismiss the appeal.

Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must calculate the optimum amount of nitrogen that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of nitrogen calculated under sub-paragraph (a).

Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate (or any combination) may be spread using an injector that injects no deeper than 10 cm below the soil surface, except within 6 metres of surface water.

In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duty to assess the amount of nitrogen fertiliser to be applied each calendar year before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.
A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.

An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record details of a contingency plan to be used in the event that an agreement for a person to accept the livestock manure fails.

The information required under paragraph (1)(j) need not be included in a risk map where the occupier does not intend to spread manure on land that has a low run-off risk during the storage period referred to in regulation 25.
Where fuel from a tank is delivered through a permanently attached flexible pipe, the pipe must be locked in a way that ensures it is kept within the bund when not in use.
Having determined an application, the Agency must notify the applicant in writing of its determination.

Incorporating organic manure and manufactured fertiliser into the soil within 12 hours of, or as soon as possible after, application is an example of a reasonable precaution for the purposes of compliance with regulation 4(3).
Enhanced nutrient management requirements apply to holdings in accordance with Regulations 4A and 4B as set out in Schedule 1A.
Where a person uses equipment to spread slurry by broadcasting, the equipment must have a trajectory of less than 4 metres from the ground.
A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must have at least 750 mm of freeboard.
For poultry manure, 30% of the total nitrogen in the livestock manure is assumed to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
Throughout the year concerned, the total amount of nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser applied to the holding must not exceed 90 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
The occupier of a holding who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.
For the purpose of regulation 5(2)(a), nitrogen levels may be determined by means of assessment of the soil nitrogen supply, rather than by the sampling and analysis of soil.
The Secretary of State may issue guidance to the Agency with respect to the exercise of the Agency's functions under these Regulations.
The Agency may at any time withdraw a notice served under regulation 7.
The land manager must ensure that a livestock feeder is not positioned on agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
Any reference in regulation 6(2) to the period stated in a notice means that period as extended if it has been extended under regulation 7(5)(b) or by virtue of regulation 8(6).
A derogation holder must plan the spreading of phosphate fertiliser as a condition of the derogation.
A person guilty of an offence under regulation 41 is liable on conviction on indictment to a fine.

Slurry or liquid from the treatment of sewage sludge by anaerobic digestion applied to the surface of bare soil or stubble must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest, unless it was applied using equipment described in regulation 17(4)(a) or (c) or an injector which injects the organic manure into the ground.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the quantity to be spread, the month in which it is to be spread, and the type of manure.
A reference to a slurry storage system includes a slurry storage tank and any reception pit and any effluent tank used in connection with the tank.
From the end of the closed period until the end of February, the maximum amount of poultry manure that may be spread at any one time is 8 tonnes per hectare.
Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February, the maximum amount of slurry that may be spread at any one time is 30 cubic metres per hectare.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be located within the bund.
The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 1999 (insofar as they remain in force) are revoked.
Parts 3 to 8 apply only in relation to holdings that are in nitrate vulnerable zones designated for the purposes of these Regulations.
A notice must state the period within which any requirement contained in it is to be complied with.

Each sample must be taken from a vessel; however, where a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, samples may instead be taken while spreading, with each sample taken at intervals during the spreading.
Any person who contravenes any provision of these Regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction, or on conviction on indictment, to a fine.
An exempt structure to which regulation 5(a) circumstances apply shall cease to be an exempt structure if it is substantially enlarged.
If the size of the holding or the area of grass within it changes, the occupier must update the record within one month beginning with the day after the change.
Where the application is of livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure), the total annual amount of manure applied must not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.
In the case of winter oilseed rape, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.

The duty to store slurry in a compliant slurry storage system does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker with a capacity not exceeding 18,000 litres used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must take into account changes and factors unforeseen at the time of the previous designation.
The occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the date on which it was brought onto the holding.
A person who contravenes regulation 32 is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale.
Regulation 32 does not apply to crops in a greenhouse.

In regulations 20 and 21, 'organic manure with high readily available nitrogen' means organic manure in which more than 30% of the total nitrogen content is available to the crop at the time of spreading.

At least every four years, the Secretary of State must review the effectiveness of the restrictions in nitrate vulnerable zones imposed by these Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources, and if necessary revise those restrictions.

'Cultivated agricultural land' means agricultural land which has been cultivated by physical means (including ploughing, sowing or harvesting) at least once in the previous year, or by chemical means (including the application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser) at least once in the previous 3 years.
No person may spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.
"Relevant water abstraction" means the abstraction of water for use for human consumption.
The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) Regulations 1991 are revoked in so far as they relate to England.
The Secretary of State must prepare a report on the implementation of the Regulations for each relevant period.

If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under regulation 6(2)(a), the Secretary of State, when acting under regulation 4(5), must treat the relevant holding (or the part upheld) as not draining into the water concerned.

When carrying out the review under regulation 39(1)(a), the Secretary of State must take into account available scientific and technical data (particularly regarding nitrogen contributions from agricultural or other sources) and regional environmental conditions.

A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure that, where silage is compressed into bales, the bales are wrapped and sealed into impermeable membranes or enclosed in impermeable bags, and are stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter.
The requirement in paragraph (1) does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
In the case of brassica crops, an additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the closed period, up to the date of harvest.

Where samples are collected to calculate compliance with the whole farm limit for pigs and poultry, four samples for analysis must be taken in a calendar year (one per quarter) from manure heaps not more than 12 months old.
No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
A notice under regulation 12(3) must be served on the person bringing the proceedings not less than 7 clear days before the hearing of the proceedings.

Where the occupier of a qualifying grassland holding intends during the relevant period to apply a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg per hectare of the holding, they must submit a notice to NRW in accordance with regulation 4B.

The enhanced nutrient management plan must record the soil phosphorus index for each area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type, and the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser (kg) that should be spread on the crop taking into account the soil phosphorus index.
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must extend beyond the walls.
The plan must record the type of crop.
A person who contravenes regulation 3(1) or (4), 4(1), 5(1) or 7(4A) is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
The Secretary of State must identify those with an interest in being consulted, including non-governmental organisations promoting environmental protection.
Regulation 32 applies to any silo or slurry storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 28 April 2021.

Where an occupier spreads organic manure using precision spreading equipment up to 6 metres from surface water as permitted by regulation 14(1), the risk map must identify land within 6 metres of surface waters.

Nitrate concentration must be measured by subtracting the amount of nitrite from the amount of total oxidised nitrogen (TON), where both nitrite and TON are calculated using molecular absorption spectrophotometry.
In paragraph (4), the 'authority' means the Agency or the Secretary of State.
The base of a slurry storage tank must be impermeable.
For the purposes of regulation 8, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14.
A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure the silage is kept in a silo that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 1.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system in relation to which a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1 March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1 September 1991.
The closed period for tillage land is the period beginning 1st September and ending the following 15th January.

A requirement for a silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or any other product to comply with a specified standard is satisfied by compliance with a relevant standard or code of practice of a national standards body or equivalent body of any EEA State, in so far as it enables the pollution prevention objectives of the Regulation to be met in an equivalent manner.
For the purposes of regulation 5(1) and (2), the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 9 for establishing nitrogen content.

A temporary field site must not be in a field liable to flooding or becoming waterlogged, within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well, within 10 metres of surface water or a land drain (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), located in any single position for more than 12 consecutive months, or located in the same place as an earlier one constructed within the last two years.

The occupier of a qualifying grassland holding must ensure that during the relevant period the total nitrogen from grazing livestock manure applied to the holding does not exceed the limit calculated by the formula A≥Ngl/250±Nngl/170.
A water supply source is a protected water supply source if the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the making of the silage began.

Where the amount of storage capacity of a holding changes, the occupier of the holding must update the record required by regulation 36(1)(b) of the old Regulations, or by regulation 25B of these Regulations, within one week.
Poultry manure must be incorporated as soon as practicable, and within 24 hours at the latest.

A person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed period on a crop not specified in the table in regulation 22(5) only if the spreading is in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser.

statements.statement_text: The occupier must make a record of the expected number of livestock animals to be kept on the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates, and the category for each animal by reference to the categories in Schedule 1.
An application must be submitted between 1 October and 31 December in the calendar year preceding the year to which the application relates.

The Agency may accept an enforcement undertaking in relation to an offence under regulation 41, as if it were an offence in relation to which that sanction was specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.
The daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production figures for grazing livestock set out in Table 1 of Schedule 1 apply for the purposes of Regulations 3, 4, 29, 34 and 36.
The fertilisation plan must record the amount of nitrogen calculated under regulation 10(1)(a) and the method used to calculate that figure.
A person must not spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water, except where permitted by paragraph (2) or (4).

A notice issued under the relevant provision may include a requirement to establish and implement a Farm Waste Management Plan in accordance with the code of practice approved under section 51(1) of the Control of Pollution Act 1974.

The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and of any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.
Solid poultry manure that does not have bedding mixed into it and is stored on a temporary field site must be covered with an impermeable material.

In any other case, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greatest of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the fuel storage tank or, where there is more than one, the largest tank within the area; (ii) where there is more than one fuel storage tank, 25 per cent of the total volume of oil that could be stored in all tanks within the area; or (iii) 25 per cent of the total volume of fuel oil at any time stored within the area.
Having determined an appeal under regulation 38, the panel must as soon as reasonably practicable notify in writing the Agency, the appellant and the Secretary of State of its determination.

The fertilisation plan must record the amount of phosphorus calculated under paragraph 3(1)(a) and the method used to calculate that figure, and the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop taking into account that phosphorus amount.
A temporary field site must not be located on land having a slope of 12 degrees or more which is within 30 metres of surface water.

If any part of an effluent tank is below ground level, the tank must be designed and constructed so that it is likely to continue to satisfy the structural integrity and impermeability requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 for at least 20 years without maintenance.
Where the panel refuses an appeal under regulation 38, it must give the reasons for its refusal.

An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must produce and maintain a risk map showing each field with its area in hectares, all surface waters, boreholes/springs/wells on or within 50 metres of the holding boundary, areas with sandy or shallow soils, land with an incline greater than 12 degrees, land within 10 metres of surface waters, land within 50 metres of a borehole/spring/well, land drains (other than sealed impermeable pipes), sites suitable for temporary field heaps, and land with a low run-off risk.

Where a storage area contains no fuel storage tank, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 25 per cent of the total volume of fuel oil at any time stored within the area.
The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels, and reception pit must be impermeable.
The duty to produce and maintain a risk map under regulation 15(1) does not apply to a holding on which organic manure is spread only in a greenhouse.

No person may spread nitrogen fertiliser on land if there is a significant risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, having regard in particular to the slope of the land (especially if more than 12°).
The Secretary of State must keep under review the eutrophic state of fresh surface waters, estuarial waters and coastal waters.

Spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed periods on crops not listed in Schedule 4 is permitted where the spreading is carried out on the basis of written advice from a person who is a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme.

statements.statement_text: The occupier must ensure that sites where supplementary feeding for livestock are provided are not located within 20 metres of a watercourse on any land during the relevant period.
Throughout the year concerned, the total amount of nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser applied to the holding must not exceed 90 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure that, where silage is compressed into bales, the bales are wrapped and sealed in impermeable membranes or enclosed in impermeable bags, and are stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter.
An occupier who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.
On all other soils, the closed period for spreading slurry or manure on tillage land runs from 1st October to the following 31st January.

The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs grass on soils that are not sandy soils on the holding before 16 January 2024 where livestock manure has been spread on that grass within the period beginning with 15 October in the previous calendar year and ending with 15 January 2024.
Regulation 31 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.
In the case of winter oilseed rape, nitrogen must not be spread after 31 October.
Each valve on a drainage pipe must be capable of shutting off the flow of slurry through the pipe, and must be kept shut and locked when not in use.

An occupier must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser and nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure, in the growing season in which it is spread (calculated in accordance with regulation 9), does not in any 12-month period exceed the limits set out in regulation 10.
Land has a 'low run-off risk' for the purposes of regulation 25 if it is at least 50 metres from a watercourse or conduit leading to a watercourse.

In assessing adequate storage capacity under sub-paragraphs (1) and (2), regard must be had to: (a) the storage capacity of any other slurry storage tank on the premises; (b) likely quantities of rainfall (including snow, hail or sleet) falling or draining into the tank during the likely maximum storage period; and (c) the need to provide not less than 750 mm freeboard for earth-walled tanks and 300 mm freeboard in all other cases.

The period for compliance with a notice under regulation 8 shall be extended so that it expires on the date on which the Scottish Ministers finally determine the appeal, or, if the appeal is withdrawn, the date on which it is withdrawn.
An expression used in regulation 13(1) and in the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 has the same meaning in regulation 13(1) as it has in that Order.

An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the type and amount of livestock manure, the date on which it was sent off the holding, the nitrogen content, the name and address of the recipient, and details of a contingency plan to be used in the event that an agreement for a person to accept the livestock manure fails.

The permitted amounts of nitrogen (kg) for specified crops are: autumn/early winter sown wheat 220 kg/ha; spring-sown wheat 180 kg/ha; winter barley 180 kg/ha; spring barley 150 kg/ha; winter oilseed rape 250 kg/ha; sugar beet 120 kg/ha; potatoes 270 kg/ha; forage maize 150 kg/ha; field beans 0 kg/ha; peas 0 kg/ha; grass 300 kg/ha; asparagus/carrots/radishes/swedes 180 kg/ha; celery/courgettes/dwarf beans/lettuce/onions/parsnips/runner beans/sweetcorn/turnips 280 kg/ha; beetroot/Brussels sprouts/cabbage/calabrese/cauliflower/leeks 370 kg/ha.

The reference to the supplier's technical analyses in paragraph (4)(a) means technical analyses carried out by the supplier and either provided to the occupier concerned or otherwise published by the supplier.
Regulation 10 of the Environmental Civil Sanctions (Miscellaneous Amendments) (England) Regulations 2010 is revoked.

Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure sent off the holding, or spread on land that has a low run-off risk in accordance with the restrictions on spreading in these Regulations; but in either case storage facilities for an additional one week's manure must be provided as a contingency measure in the event of spreading not being possible on some dates.
Where manure is applied using precision spreading equipment, the land manager must ensure that the manure is not applied within 6 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
SEPA may at any time withdraw a notice served under regulation 8.
A person on whom a regulation 30 notice has been served must comply with the requirements of that notice.
The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year using the Table in Schedule 1.
For pig slurry, 50% of the total nitrogen in the livestock manure is assumed to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
The occupier must keep a copy of the risk map.
For the purposes of regulation 13, the total amount of nitrogen from organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14 for establishing available nitrogen.

An occupier of a holding who has submitted an undertaking to the organic farming control system under Article 27 of Council Regulation (EC) 834/2007 may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen at any time on other crops, provided that spreading is in accordance with written advice from a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme.

statements.statement_text: Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under regulation 11, and the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of an officer, or to have been attributable to any neglect on the part of an officer, that officer is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
The Secretary of State must from time to time carry out a review of the regulatory provision contained in these Regulations and publish a report setting out the conclusions of the review.
An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must produce and maintain a risk map of the holding showing each field with its area in hectares.

Where organic manure (other than livestock manure) is supplied by a manufacturer or other supplier, the nitrogen content and available nitrogen must be calculated by reference to the supplier's technical analyses, or where such information is unavailable, by reference to the values given in the Fertiliser Manual (referred to there as 'total nitrogen' and 'nitrogen available for the next crop' respectively).

The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
Regulation 20 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser in a greenhouse.
In regulation 25, 'storage period' means, in any case other than pigs and poultry, the period that begins with 1st October and ends with the following 1st March.
The occupier must maintain the holding to ensure at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the calendar year to which the derogation applies.
A land manager must ensure that poaching is prevented within 5 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
Slurry and liquid digested sewage sludge must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable, and within 24 hours at the latest, after application.
The compliance period stated in an enforcement notice must be such period as SEPA considers reasonable, but must not end earlier than 28 days after the day on which the notice is served.
These Regulations extend to Scotland only.

The period for compliance with a notice under regulation 8 is automatically extended so that it expires on the date on which the Scottish Ministers finally determine the appeal or, if the appeal is withdrawn, the date on which it is withdrawn, subject to any direction under regulation 9(5).

The fertilisation account must record the number and category of animals kept on the holding during the relevant period in accordance with Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1, and the amount of nitrogen and phosphate (kg) in the manure produced by those animals during the relevant period using those Tables.

Where the affairs of a body corporate are managed by its members, the liability provisions applicable to officers of a body corporate apply equally to a member in connection with that member's functions of management.
Any period for compliance stated in a notice must be such period as SEPA considers reasonable in the circumstances, and must not end earlier than 28 days after the day on which the notice is served.

A person required to make a record under these Regulations must keep that record for a period of 5 years after the record ceased to be current, regardless of whether the land has in the meantime ceased to be designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone.
The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels, and reception pit must be impermeable.
For the purposes of regulation 10(5), 'land management and cultivation practices' includes irrigating crops or spraying them with pesticides, herbicides or fungicides.
A person must not spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on land during the closed period.

As part of the review under regulation 39, the Secretary of State must review the overall position of derogations granted under this regulation against the objective of preventing further water pollution caused or induced by nitrates from agricultural sources.

The provisions of the Transfrontier Shipment of Waste Regulations 2007 relating to the sanctions referred to in paragraph (1) apply as if they were provisions of the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015.
The occupier of a new holding must record the total size of the holding, calculated in accordance with regulation 7(4).
The occupier must maintain the holding to ensure that at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the relevant period.

Where the Agency refuses an application under regulation 36, the occupier may appeal against the refusal by notice to an independent panel appointed by the Secretary of State for the purpose of these Regulations.

All remaining provisions of the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010 are revoked in relation to all other holdings (not situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone) on 1 August 2024.

At least every four years, the Welsh Ministers must review the effectiveness of the measures imposed by these Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution from agricultural sources and, if necessary, revise them.
In assessing the significant risk of nitrogen entering surface water, account must be taken of the soil type and the presence of land drains.

A person served with a notice under regulation 8 may appeal to the Scottish Ministers against the notice within 28 days beginning with the day on which that notice is served, or within such longer period as the Scottish Ministers may allow.
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the date of spreading.

In any other case (fuel oil stored in containers other than tanks), the bund must be capable of retaining the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest container, or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil at any time stored within the area.

The base and walls of the slurry storage tank, any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7 of BS 5502: Part 50:1993.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen spread on a crop or group of crops specified in the table in regulation 12(4) does not exceed the permitted figure (adjusted per the notes and multiplied by the total area in hectares of the crop or group sown on the holding) in any twelve-month period.
The factors to be considered under paragraph (2) include those specified in regulation 4(2).
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must extend beyond the walls.

Where a silo has retaining walls, those retaining walls must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraphs 15.6.1 to 15.6.3 of BS 5502 (Part 22: 1993).

If a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on the pipe, with each valve separated from the other by a minimum distance of 1 metre.

For the purposes of regulation 4(5)(a), in point A(1) of Annex 1 to Council Directive 91/676/EEC, the words from 'more than' to 'Directive 75/440/EEC' are to be read as if substituted by 'a concentration of nitrates greater than 50 mg/l'.

The Agency may impose a fixed monetary penalty, variable monetary penalty, restoration notice, compliance notice or stop notice, or may accept an enforcement undertaking, in relation to an offence under regulation 41, as if it were an offence specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.

The closed period for grassland with sandy or shallow soil is 1st September to the following 31st December; for grassland with all other soils it is 15th October to the following 31st January. The closed period for tillage land with sandy or shallow soil is 1st August to the following 31st December; for tillage land with all other soils it is 1st October to the following 31st January.
Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be spread only during the period beginning 1st June and ending the following 31st October.
In the Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, paragraph 24 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 is substituted as provided by WSI 2021/77 regulation 49(2)(b).
A water supply source is a protected water supply source if any relevant water abstraction from the source is licensed under Part II of the Water Resources Act 1991.
Land has a 'low run-off risk' for the purposes of regulation 25 if it has an average slope of less than 3 degrees.

If the occupier of a holding introduces animals onto the holding for the first time, the occupier must, within one month of the introduction, calculate and record: (a) the amount of manure that will be produced by the expected number of animals kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period using Schedule 1 figures; (b) the storage capacity required to comply with regulation 25, accounting for manure to be exported, manure to be spread on low run-off risk land, and liquids other than slurry likely to enter a slurry vessel; and (c) the current storage capacity of the holding.

In the case of any crop other than permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the fertilisation plan duty before spreading nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or intended to be planted.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must on each occasion calculate the amount of nitrogen that is likely to be available from that manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must on each occasion calculate the amount of nitrogen from that manure that is likely to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not stored on agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
"Water supply source" means inland freshwaters or ground waters from which a relevant abstraction is made or licensed to be made.
In carrying out the review, the Secretary of State must have regard to how Council Directive 91/676/EEC is implemented in other member States.
Where an occupier intends to spread slurry on the holding during the relevant period, precision spreading equipment must be used, except where it would not be reasonably practicable to do so.
The risk map must show all surface waters, any boreholes, springs or wells on the holding or within 50 metres of the boundary of the holding, and areas with sandy or shallow soils.
The Agency must have regard to any guidance issued under paragraph (1) in the exercise of its functions.
The occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the name and address of the supplier.
In regulation 25, 'storage period' means, in the case of pigs and poultry, the period that begins with 1st October and ends with the following 1st April.

If the Welsh Ministers are satisfied that proposals submitted under regulation 45(1) would be more effective in delivering the outcomes in regulation 44(1), they must publish a statement within two years of these Regulations coming into force explaining what action will be taken.
In regulation 40A, 'relevant period' means the period of four years beginning with 1st January 2016 and each successive period of four years.
Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as a species-rich semi-natural grassland only if that land comes within paragraph (3).
Before the relevant date every year, the occupier must make a record of the number of days that each animal spent on the holding during the previous 12-month period.

In the case of any crop other than permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duties under paragraph 3(1) before spreading phosphate fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or to be planted.
For the purposes of regulation 36(2), paragraph 2(b) of Annex 3 to Council Directive 91/676/EEC is to be read as if the third subparagraph were omitted.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the name and address of the recipient.
The base of a silo must be designed in accordance with BS 8007:1987 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for design of concrete structures for retaining aqueous liquids).
Regulation 9 applies to any silo, slurry or fuel oil storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 15th June 2013.
A reference to a slurry storage system includes any channels and pipes used in connection with the tank, any reception pit, or any effluent tank.
An application must be made in the form and manner published by the Secretary of State.
The Agency has the function of enforcing these Regulations.
Regulation 16 does not apply to land which is covered by a greenhouse.

Subject to regulation 6, no person having custody or control of any crop being made into silage or of any silage being stored may keep it otherwise than in a silo satisfying the requirements of Schedule 1 or which is an exempt structure under regulation 5.
Where precision spreading equipment is used, no person may spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water during the relevant period.
A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.

Where a sampling station has recorded nitrate concentrations below 25mg/l in all previous samples taken under regulation 4(2) and no new factor likely to increase nitrate content has appeared, the monitoring obligation in regulation 4(2) is modified so that the reference to '2017' is read as '2021' and the reference to 'every four years' is read as 'every eight years'.

Where land has been harvested using a combine harvester, forage harvester or mower, the occupier must ensure that throughout the relevant period (beginning the first day after harvest and ending 31 December 2024) the stubble of the harvested crop remains in the land.

On determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers may direct NRW to withdraw the regulation 30 notice, modify any of its requirements, extend the period for compliance with any requirement, or dismiss the appeal.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not applied to agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
The occupier must, before spreading organic manure, record the planned date (month) for spreading and the type of organic manure.

Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 75% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the grant of the derogation.
At least ten samples of 1 kg each must be taken from a solid manure heap, each from a different location in the heap.
Regulation 9 applies to any silo, slurry or fuel oil storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 15th June 2013.

Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record the number of animals on the holding during the previous calendar year and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1, and the number of days that each animal spent on the holding.

After acting in reliance on regulation 13, the occupier must provide the FACTS adviser with soil analyses from representative autumn soil samples so that the adviser may take the analyses into account when advising for the purposes of paragraph (2) in relation to subsequent years.

statements.statement_text: The reference to 'land on the holding' in paragraph (1) does not include any land which is covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the period concerned.

Before determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers shall, if requested by the appellant or SEPA, afford them an opportunity of appearing before and being heard by a person appointed by the Scottish Ministers for that purpose.

A silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank or container is an exempt structure if it was an exempt structure under the 2001 Regulations and had not ceased to be an exempt structure on the date immediately before the coming into force of these Regulations.

A requirement for a silo or slurry storage tank to conform to a British Standard is satisfied if the silo or tank conforms to a standard or specification that provides an equivalent level of protection and performance and is recognised for use in a member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Turkey.

A person is regarded as having been found in breach of the derogation conditions where a penalty or notice has been imposed under regulation 42 in relation to such an offence and either no further appeal may be made against the penalty or notice or, where there was an appeal, it was decided against the person.

A water supply source is a protected water supply source for the purposes of regulation 24(1)(c)(ii) if the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the making of the silage began.
In a holding or part of a holding not previously situated within a nitrate vulnerable zone, regulations 5 to 11, 15, 23, 27, 33 to 35, and 37 to 43 do not apply until 1 January 2023.
An appeal under regulation 38 must be submitted before the end of 30 days beginning with the day after the date of the refusal.

A regulation 30 notice must specify or describe the required works, precautions or other steps; state the period for compliance (being 28 days or such longer period as is reasonable); and inform the person of the effect of regulation 31.

A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure the silage is kept in a silo satisfying the requirements of Schedule 5, or compressed into bales that are wrapped and sealed in impermeable membranes or enclosed in impermeable bags and stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter.
At least every four years, the Secretary of State must, if necessary, revise the restrictions in nitrate vulnerable zones imposed by these Regulations.
For brassica crops, the maximum nitrogen application rate during the closed period is 100 kg/hectare.

The total amount of phosphate spread on any crop listed in Table 2 (grass) or Table 3 (other crops) must not exceed the figure under the applicable soil phosphorus index number in the respective table.
Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must ascertain it as soon as is reasonably practicable after arrival.
The occupier of a holding may apply to the Agency for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area of the holding is sown with grass.
Before 30th April each year, the occupier of a holding must record how any grassland was managed in the previous calendar year.
Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must undertake a field inspection to consider the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.

Where a silo has a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more, the capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres.
The Secretary of State must carry out a review of these Regulations from time to time, in so far as not already done under regulation 39.

For potatoes, the maximum phosphate application rates (kg P₂O₅/ha) by soil phosphorus index are: 250 (index 0), 210 (1), 170 (2), 100 (3), 0 (4), 0 (5+); these figures form part of Table 3 governing maximum phosphate for other crops.

Where sowing within the 10-day period following final seedbed preparation would lead to a significant risk of soil erosion and nitrogen or phosphorus entering a surface water, the crop or temporary cover crop must be sown as soon as is practicable after the land ceases to be waterlogged.
Regulation 4(1) does not apply where the total quantity of fuel oil stored on the farm does not exceed 1,250 litres.

A person who contravenes regulation 3(1) of the Regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.

The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010 are revoked, in relation to a holding or part of a holding situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone as shown on the Nitrate Vulnerable Zones Index Map 2013, on 1 April 2021.
Monitoring of nitrate concentration in freshwaters at sampling stations representative of surface water must be carried out at least monthly and more frequently during flood periods.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in drums within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.
For the purposes of regulation 2(4), 'authority' means the Environment Agency or the Secretary of State.
An appeal under regulation 8 must be made by the appellant serving notice on the Secretary of State.

Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the soil likely to be available for crop uptake during the growing season, calculate the optimum amount of nitrogen to be spread taking that figure into account, and produce a fertilisation plan for that growing season.
The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Designation and Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2013 are revoked.
Throughout the year concerned, the occupier must not bring organic manure on to the holding.
Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system which, before 1 March 1991, was being used for the purpose of making silage or storing slurry.
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser within 2 metres of surface water.
The occupier must record the total agricultural area and the area of grass within the holding by 1 March 2024.
Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) must not be spread directly onto surface water.

The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) Regulations 2013, the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) (Amendment) Regulations 2015, and the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) (Amendment) Regulations 2019 are revoked.
Regulation 7(1) does not apply where the occupier has been granted a derogation.

A person who has custody or control of field silage or silage stored on open land must give NRW notice of the place where the silage is to be made or stored at least 14 days before the place is first used for that purpose.
The total annual amount of livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) spread must not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system in relation to which construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was commenced before 1 March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1 September 1991.
The base of a silo must be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo.

No person having custody or control of any crop made into silage in the manner described in regulation 6(1) shall open or empty any bag in which silage has been made unless that person does so at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
The permitted amount of nitrogen (kg/ha) for autumn or early winter sown wheat is 220 kg, with a standard yield of 8 tonne/ha.
The occupier of a holding must, within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, record: (a) the date of spreading, and (b) the amount of nitrogen spread.

In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may alternatively use software approved by the Welsh Ministers, or, where the system of keeping livestock produces only solid manure, sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3, instead of the Schedule 1 Table calculation.
The Agency must withdraw a regulation 7 notice, extend the period for compliance, or modify the requirements of the notice if so directed by the Secretary of State under regulation 8(5).
The permitted amount of nitrogen for field beans and peas is 0 kg per hectare (no standard yield applies).
In the case of winter oilseed rape, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
A notice must state the period within which any such requirement is to be complied with.
A notice under regulation 5(3)(b) or 5(3A)(b) must contain information about other means of obtaining the relevant information that do not require access to the internet.
A person who contravenes regulation 3(1) or (4), 4(1), 5(1) or 7(4A) is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction on indictment to a fine.
All nitrogen content of livestock manure must be ascertained using either the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 3 or by sampling and analysis as set out in Part 2 of that Schedule.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in an underground fuel storage tank.
Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in regulation 15(1), the occupier must update the risk map within three months of the change.

If proposals for an alternative suite of measures for delivering the outcomes in regulation 44(1) are received within 18 months of these Regulations coming into force, the Welsh Ministers must consider whether those measures would deliver the outcomes more effectively than the measures contained in these Regulations.
An occupier who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must record the date of sowing within one week of sowing a crop.
The Agency must make provision for a relevant map to be obtainable by persons without access to the internet.

Before the relevant date every year, the occupier must make a record of the number and category of animals on the holding during the previous 12-month period and the number of days each animal spent on the holding.

For agricultural land to which the livestock feeder exclusion zones do not apply, the land manager must ensure that any factors which mean there would be a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution are taken into account when deciding where to locate a livestock feeder, including the factors in regulation 4(2).
The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.
If the size of the holding changes, the record must be updated within one month of that change.
The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser (kg) that should be spread on the crop during the relevant period, taking into account the soil phosphorus index.

An occupier of a holding who keeps any animals specified in column 1 of Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all poultry manure produced in a yard or building on the holding during the storage period.
For cattle slurry, 40% of the total nitrogen in the livestock manure is assumed to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.

A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.

The occupier may exceed the 250kg nitrogen limit where: (1) the organic manure is certified green compost or certified green/food compost; (2) the total nitrogen from such compost does not exceed 500kg per hectare in any two-year period (or 1,000kg per hectare in any four-year period for orchard land spread as mulch); and (3) no other form of organic manure is spread over the land during the applicable period.
The first report must be published before 2nd April 2021.
No person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on grassland with all other soils (not sandy or shallow) between 15 October and 15 January (inclusive).

Where the Agency refuses an application under regulation 36, the occupier may appeal against the refusal to an independent panel appointed by the Secretary of State, and such appeal must be submitted within 30 days beginning with the day after the date of the refusal.
A notice of appeal must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal.

The Agency must refuse a derogation application where the occupier has been found in breach of the derogation conditions during the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates, subject to the discretion in paragraph (8).
A land manager must ensure that a livestock feeder is not positioned on agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters, or within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.

A report under regulation 40A(1) must be published in such manner as the Secretary of State considers appropriate and by the last day of the six-month period beginning with the day on which the relevant period ends.
Within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier must record the amount of nitrogen spread.

Schedule 1 sets out the daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate produced by each grazing livestock animal by category, for the purposes of Regulations 2(1), 7(3), 25(1) and (2), 26(1), 27(1) and (2) and 34(4) of UKSI 2015/668.
Application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser includes spreading on the surface of the land.
Subsequent reports under regulation 40 must be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years.
These Regulations apply to England only.

Crop rotation on the holding during the relevant period must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen, except for grass with less than 50% clover or any other leguminous plants that are under-sown with grass.
The total amount of nitrogen which the occupier may spread on any given hectare must not exceed 500 kg if the grass is not irrigated.

Nitrate concentration must be measured by subtracting the amount of nitrite from the amount of total oxidised nitrogen (TON), where both nitrite and TON are calculated using molecular absorption spectrophotometry.
"Relevant water abstraction" includes the abstraction of water for use for domestic purposes (within the meaning given by section 218 of the Water Industry Act 1991) other than human consumption.

No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must identify land which drains into waters identified as affected by pollution (including waters similarly identified in Wales or Scotland) and that contributes to the pollution in those waters.

Following the record-making under paragraph 17(1), the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate (kg) in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during the relevant period, using Tables 1 and 2 (as applicable) in Schedule 1.

Spreading phosphate on grass or other crops above the values stipulated in the tables in paragraph 9 is permitted only where prior written advice has been received from a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme (FACTS).
