statements.statement_text: Before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must record the month in which it is planned to spread it.
A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.
Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must record it within one week of ascertaining it.
Where the Agency has refused an application, it must give the reasons for its refusal.
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank shall extend beyond its walls.
An occupier who used software approved by the Welsh Ministers must keep a printout of the result.

Where the occupier of a qualifying grassland holding intends during the relevant period to apply a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares, the occupier must comply with the enhanced nutrient management requirements in Schedule 1A.

In calculating the area of the holding for the purposes of ascertaining the amount of nitrogen to be spread on the holding, no account is taken of surface waters, any hardstanding, buildings, roads or any woodland, unless that woodland is used for grazing.

For each area planted or intended to be planted, the nutrient management plan must record the optimum amount of nitrogen that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of nitrogen available from the soil nitrogen supply.

The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of soil phosphorus calculated under paragraph 3(1)(a), and must produce a plan for the spreading of phosphate fertiliser for that growing season.
Where the occupier uses software approved by the Secretary of State, the occupier must keep a printout of the result.
The occupier must record the temporary field sites used for free-standing heaps and the dates of use.

Where silage is a crop being made into field silage or silage being stored on open land, the person with custody or control must give NRW at least 14 days' notice of the place before it is first used, and the place must be at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant water abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage effluent could enter if it escaped.
The occupier must record the sites used for field heaps and the dates of use.

NRW may serve a notice on a person who has custody or control of silage or slurry, or is responsible for a silo or slurry storage system, requiring that person to carry out works or take precautions or other steps specified in the notice.
The occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the nitrogen content of the livestock manure if known.
A temporary field site must not be in a field liable to flooding or becoming waterlogged.

No part of a slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels, pipes or reception pit shall be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which slurry could enter if it were to escape.

Where the occupier of a qualifying grassland holding intends during the relevant period to apply a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg per hectare of the holding, they must comply with the enhanced nutrient management requirements in Schedule 1A.

These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank in relation to which a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1st March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1st September 1991.

When planning the application of agricultural diffuse pollution sources, the land manager must ensure that the presence and condition of any agricultural land drains is taken into account as a factor indicating significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
If the size of the holding or the area of grass within it changes, the occupier must update the record within one month beginning with the day after the day of the change.

Slurry and liquid digested sewage sludge applied onto the surface of bare soil or stubble must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest, unless applied using equipment of a type described in regulation 14(4).
Any reference in regulation 7(1) to the period stated in a notice means that period as extended if it has been extended under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5) or (6).
In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with paragraph (1) each year beginning 1 January before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.
Where a silo has retaining walls, notices must be displayed on the retaining walls in accordance with paragraph 18 of BS 5502: Part 22: 2003.

In relation to an offence under regulation 11(1), the Agency may impose a restoration notice, compliance notice, stop notice, fixed monetary penalty, variable monetary penalty, or accept an enforcement undertaking, as if it were an offence in relation to which the sanction in question was specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.
When carrying out the review, the Secretary of State must ensure that the public are given early and effective opportunities to participate in the review.

The 10-metre buffer zone does not apply to the application of livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) where the manure is applied in the period beginning on 1 June and ending on 31 October, is not applied directly onto the surface of inland freshwaters or coastal waters, and the total annual amount applied does not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.
The obligation in paragraph (1) applies only in so far as there is a change in the area of the land on the holding that is not covered by a greenhouse.
A person may spread fertiliser during the closed period on a crop specified in the table in paragraph (5) provided the rate of nitrogen specified in the second column of that table is not exceeded.

A notice under regulation 4B must be submitted to NRW by 31 March 2024, accompanied by the enhanced nutrient management plan for the qualifying grassland holding, and both must be submitted by e-mail.
Solid poultry manure that does not have bedding mixed into it and is stored on a temporary field site must be covered with an impermeable material.

Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow out of the channel is controlled by a sluice, the reception pit must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
Regulation 14 sets out the method for calculating the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure (nitrogen content) for the purposes of regulations 8(9), 12(2), 13(4) and 31(6).
The occupier of a qualifying grassland holding must ensure that during the relevant period the total grassland area satisfies the formula A≥Ngl/250±Nngl/170.

Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on a farm in any two-day period (disregarding slurry transferred directly into a slurry storage tank).
These Regulations apply in relation to Wales.

The occupier must, before spreading organic manure, record the total nitrogen content and the amount of nitrogen likely to be available from the organic manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.

A requirement for a silo or slurry storage tank to conform to a British Standard is satisfied if the silo or tank conforms to a standard or specification that provides an equivalent level of protection and performance and is recognised for use in a member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Turkey.
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulations 10 to 13 commits an offence.
The references in paragraphs (1) and (3) to 'the old regulations' mean the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008.
Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record the number of days that each animal spent on the holding during the previous calendar year.
In carrying out the review, the Secretary of State must have regard to how Council Directive 91/676/EEC is implemented in other member States.
The fertilisation plan must record the area of the field planted or intended to be planted.
These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which, before 1st March 1991, was being used for the purpose of making silage, storing slurry or storing fuel oil.
Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must undertake a field inspection to consider the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.

Where the exemptions in regulation 29(4)(a) or (b) apply, storage facilities for an additional one week's manure must be provided as a contingency measure in the event of spreading not being possible on some dates.
An expression used in regulation 42(1) and in the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Order has the same meaning in that paragraph as it has in that Order.

Where no nitrogen content value is established for an organic manure for the purposes of the relevant provision, the occupier may not spread that manure in reliance on that provision on a crop referred to in regulation 12 or 13.
Schedule 4 lists the permitted crops for the closed period together with their maximum nitrogen application rates (kg/hectare), as referenced by Regulations 20 and 22.
The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the date and method of spreading.

An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record the type and amount, the date it is sent off, the nitrogen content, the name and address of the recipient, and details of a contingency plan in the event that an agreement for a person to accept the livestock manure fails.
References to 'application' of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser include injection into the land and mixing with the surface layers of the soil.

Regulation 2 shall not apply where a person makes bulk bagged silage on a farm in bags that are made of 1000 gauge polyethylene or material of at least equivalent impermeability and durability, are kept sealed to prevent the escape of silage effluent, and are stored on a firm level surface incorporating a facility designed to enable the safe removal of excess effluent when present.
A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain details of any steps taken to promote good agricultural practice.

Where technical analyses from the supplier are unavailable, the occupier must establish nitrogen available for crop uptake in other organic manure by reference to the values given in the Nutrient Management Guide (RB209), or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3.

No part of a slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions are taken that the Agency agrees in writing are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.

These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank in relation to which construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was commenced before 1st March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1st September 1991.
Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure that is sent off the holding.
The Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Amendment) Regulations 1997 are revoked in so far as they relate to England.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage or slurry to be kept in a new or improved store must give NRW notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location, at least 14 days before work constructing the store is to be begun.
The occupier must ensure that in the calendar year for which the derogation has effect, the conditions specified in paragraph (1) are met.
The occupier of a holding must ensure that in any twelve-month period, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure spread on any given hectare of land on the holding does not exceed 250kg.

An occupier of a holding who keeps any of the animals specified in Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period, and all poultry manure produced in a yard or building on the holding during the storage period.

In relation to all organic manure other than that covered by regulation 9(1)–(2), the occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread, by reference to technical analyses provided by the supplier.
These Regulations come into force on 6th April 2010.
The fertilisation plan must record the soil type in relation to the area planted or intended to be planted.
For the purposes of paragraph 10, a crop with high nitrogen demand includes grass, potatoes, sugar beet, maize, wheat, oilseed rape, barley, brassica, rye and triticale.
For the purposes of regulation 7, the amount of nitrogen must be calculated in accordance with Schedule 1.

'Agri-environmental commitment' means any commitment entered into under Council Regulation (EC) No. 1698/2005 or Regulation (EU) No. 1305/2013 on support for rural development by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development.

For the purposes of regulation 12, 'total amount of nitrogen' means the sum of (a) nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser and (b) nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure in the growing season in which it is spread, calculated in accordance with regulation 14.

If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under regulation 6(2)(b), the Secretary of State when acting under regulation 4(5) must treat any holding (or part of any holding) which drains into that water accordingly, regardless of whether the owner or occupier of the relevant holding appealed under this regulation.
The occupier of a holding must, within one week of sowing a crop on which the occupier spreads or intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser, record the crop sown and the date of sowing.
In the case of grass, a maximum of 40kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time.

Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank may have a lesser capacity than the two-day maximum where NRW agrees in writing that the lesser capacity is adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
The occupier must keep a copy of the risk map for the holding.
Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February, the maximum amount of poultry manure that may be spread at any one time is 8 tonnes per hectare.

The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs grass on sandy soils on the holding before 16 January 2024 where livestock manure has been spread on that grass within the period beginning with 1 September and ending with 31 December in the previous calendar year.
Application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser includes injection into the land.

The provisions of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 (or relevant Order) relating to the sanctions specified in paragraph (1) apply to these Regulations as if those provisions were provisions of these Regulations.

For separated cattle slurry, the standard total nitrogen content varies by separation method: liquid fraction — strainer box 1.5 kg/m³, weeping wall 2 kg/m³, mechanical separator 3 kg/m³; solid fraction 4 kg/m³.
Poultry manure applied onto the surface of bare soil or stubble must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable, and within 24 hours at the latest.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system in relation to which a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1 March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1 September 1991.

Regulations 2 to 25 of the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Amendment) and Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2013 are revoked.

To the extent that technical analyses from the supplier are unavailable, the occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake by reference to the values given in the Nutrient Management Guide (RB209).

Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure spread on land that has a low run-off risk, provided that spreading is done in accordance with the restrictions on spreading in these Regulations.

In assessing the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, account must be taken in particular of: (a) the slope of the land (especially if greater than 12 degrees); (b) any ground cover; (c) the proximity to surface water; (d) the weather conditions; (e) the soil type; and (f) the presence of land drains.
An occupier of a holding who keeps any animals specified in column 1 of Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period.

Where the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones before 1st January 2017, the Secretary of State must by 31st December 2016 publish the proposals on the Agency's website, and by 1st March 2017 send written notice to any person appearing to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.
For the purpose of regulation 5(2)(a), nitrogen levels may be determined by means of assessment of the soil nitrogen supply, rather than by sampling and analysis of soil.
A report published under regulation 16 must assess whether the objectives of the regulatory provision referred to in paragraph (1)(a) remain appropriate.
No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must, if necessary, revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be shut and locked in the shut position when not in use.
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the amount of phosphate spread.
These Regulations extend to England and Wales.

Having complied with the duty under sub-paragraph (1), the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.

Before determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers must, if requested by the appellant or NRW, afford them an opportunity of appearing before and being heard by a person appointed by the Welsh Ministers for the purpose.
An expression used in regulation 42(1) and in the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 has the same meaning in regulation 42(1) as it has in that Order.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the type and amount of livestock manure.
For the purposes of paragraph (5), the area of the holding excludes any land on which the occupier does not spread fertiliser or work the soil.
Any reference in regulation 7(1) to a requirement of a notice means that requirement as modified if it has been modified under regulation 8(5) or by virtue of regulation 9(5).
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must be provided with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any slurry that escapes from the tank.

The works, precautions or other steps required must be, in the opinion of the Agency, appropriate having regard to the requirements of the Regulations, for reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
For the purposes of regulation 29, the 'storage period' in any case other than pigs and poultry is the period between 1 October and 1 March (all dates inclusive).
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must be provided with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any slurry that escapes from the tank.

Where the amount of storage capacity of a holding changes, the occupier must update the record required by regulation 36(1)(b) of the old Regulations or regulation 25B of these Regulations within one week.
The land manager must ensure that a livestock feeder is not positioned on agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
Topsoil must not be removed from the ground upon which a temporary field site is to be constructed.

The risk map must show each field with its area in hectares, all surface waters, any boreholes/springs/wells on or within 50 metres of the holding boundary, areas with sandy or shallow soils, land with an incline greater than 12°, land within 10 metres of surface waters, land within 50 metres of a borehole/spring/well, land drains (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), and sites suitable for temporary field heaps if that storage method is to be used.
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on tillage land during the closed period, which begins on 1 September and ends on the following 15 January.

Monitoring of nitrate concentration in freshwaters at sampling stations representative of groundwater must be carried out at regular intervals, taking into account the provisions of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 and the Private Water Supplies (England) Regulations 2016.

P may not rely on a due diligence defence based on reliance on information supplied by another person unless it was reasonable for P to have relied on that information, having regard to the steps taken to verify it and whether P had any reason to disbelieve it.

A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.
The occupier of a holding with livestock must maintain a record of the current capacity for storage on the holding.
A notice served under the relevant provision must specify or describe the works, precautions or other steps which the person is required to carry out or take.
A person on whom a regulation 7 notice has been served must comply with the requirements of that notice.
In the exercise of its functions, the Agency must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State under regulation 15(1).
Each party to an appeal under regulation 38 must bear its own costs.
Where a holding is designated as a derogated holding, the occupier must meet the derogation conditions in relation to that holding.
Regulation 19 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.
The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the area spread.

In Part [containing regulation 17], 'organic manure with high readily available nitrogen' means organic manure in which more than 30% of the total nitrogen content is available to the crop at the time of spreading.
Where a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, the five samples may instead be taken while spreading, with each sample taken at intervals during the spreading.

The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding, the amount of manure intended to be spread on land with a low run-off risk, and, in the case of a slurry vessel, the amount of liquids other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.
A report under paragraph (1) must be published in such manner as the Secretary of State considers appropriate.

The occupier of a holding must not store organic manure (other than slurry), or bedding contaminated with organic manure, except in a vessel, in a covered building (including a greenhouse), on an impermeable surface, or (in the case of solid manure which can be stacked in a free-standing heap and which does not drain liquid) on a temporary field site.
A land manager must ensure that manufactured fertiliser is not applied to agricultural land within two metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters, or of a spring, well or borehole.

For any crop other than permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the regulation 6(1) obligations before spreading nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or intended to be planted.

A person is regarded as having been found in breach of the derogation conditions where they have given the Agency an enforcement undertaking under regulation 42 in relation to an offence under regulation 41 arising from a breach of those conditions.

In a holding or part of a holding not previously situated within a nitrate vulnerable zone, regulations 4 and 36 do not apply until 1 January 2024, except that regulation 4 does not apply to qualifying grassland holdings until 1 January 2025.

The results of soil sampling and analysis must include the pH of the soil and the levels of nitrogen, phosphorous, magnesium and potassium present, must be no more than 5 years old at the time of the application, and may have been collected before the date on which these Regulations come into force, including by another land manager.

No person having custody or control of any crop which is being or has been made into silage in bale form shall open or remove the wrapping of any bales unless they do so at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
References to 'application' of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser include spreading on the surface of the land.
For each area planted or intended to be planted, the nutrient management plan must record the soil type.

A person served with a regulation 30 notice may appeal to the Welsh Ministers against the notice within 28 days beginning on the day after the date on which the notice is served, or such longer period as the Welsh Ministers allow.
Subsequent reports under regulation 16 must be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years.

The occupier must undertake soil sampling analysis of at least every five hectares of the agricultural area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type, for the purpose of determining the soil phosphorus index for each such area.

Where slurry is proposed to be utilised on the premises by spreading it on land, the slurry storage tank need not have a greater storage capacity than is adequate to hold the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced in any four-month period, taking into account the matters in sub-paragraph (3).
No person may spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil is waterlogged, flooded, snow covered, frozen, or has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.

An occupier may rely on the results of previous soil sampling analysis of the agricultural area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type for the purposes of paragraph 4(1), provided such sampling analysis was carried out within the period beginning with 1 January 2020 and ending with 31 December 2023.
Regulation 12 applies irrespective of the figure given in the fertilisation plan, but is subject to regulation 13.
The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be brought on to the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates.

The works, precautions or other steps required must be, in the opinion of NRW, appropriate having regard to the requirements of the Regulations, for reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.

The occupier of a holding with livestock must maintain a record of the amount of storage capacity (slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 29, taking into account: (i) the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding; (ii) the amount of manure intended to be spread on land with a low run-off risk; and (iii) in the case of a slurry vessel, the amount of liquid other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.

Subject to regulation 6, no person having custody or control of any crop being made into silage or of any silage being stored may keep it otherwise than as bales that are wrapped and sealed within impermeable membranes (or enclosed in impermeable bags) and stored at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) (Amendment) Regulations 2015 are revoked.
In the case of grass, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.

In regulation 12, 'third party allegation' means an allegation that the commission of the offence was due to the act or default of another person, or to reliance on information supplied by another person.

In relation to all other organic manure, the occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake in the growing season of spreading for the purposes of regulation 8 by reference to technical analyses provided by the supplier.

Solid manure samples must be placed on a clean, dry tray or sheet, any lumps must be broken up, and the samples must be thoroughly mixed together before a representative sample of at least 2 kg is sent for analysis.
Where a silo has retaining walls, notices must be displayed on those retaining walls in accordance with paragraph 18 of BS 5502: Part 22:2003.

If the Welsh Ministers are satisfied that proposals submitted under paragraph (1) would be more effective in delivering the outcomes in regulation 44(1), they must publish a statement within two years of these Regulations coming into force explaining what action will be taken.
A reference to a slurry storage system includes any channels and pipes used in connection with the tank, any reception pit, or any effluent tank.

Once total nitrogen in livestock manure has been determined, the following percentages are assumed to establish nitrogen available for crop uptake in the growing season of spreading: cattle slurry 40%, pig slurry 50%, poultry manure 30%, other livestock manure 10%.
In paragraph (3), 'director', in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, means a member of the body.

As part of the review under regulation 39, the Secretary of State must review the overall position of derogations granted under regulation 36 against objective criteria (including long growing seasons, high nitrogen-uptake crops, soils with exceptionally high denitrification capacity, and net rainfall in designated nitrate vulnerable zones) and against the objectives of reducing and preventing water pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources.

A person (P) may not rely on the defence under regulation 12(1) on the ground that the offence was due to reliance on information supplied by another person, unless it was reasonable for P to have relied on that information.

A requirement for a silo or slurry storage tank to conform to a British Standard is satisfied if the silo or tank conforms to a standard or specification that provides an equivalent level of protection and performance.
For other livestock manure, the available nitrogen for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread is 10% (applicable on and after 1st January 2014).
On determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers may direct SEPA to extend the period for compliance with any requirement of the notice.
A notice under regulation 4B must include a written statement that the occupier will comply with the additional requirements set out in Schedule 1A.
A person must not spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.

For the purposes of regulation 4(5)(a), each reference in Annex 1 to Council Directive 91/676/EEC to Article 5 of that Directive is to be read as a reference to regulations 7 to 35 of these Regulations.
An appeal under regulation 31 must be made by the appellant serving notice on the Welsh Ministers.

An occupier who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week, record the type and amount, the date it is brought on, the nitrogen content, and (if known) the name and address of the supplier.

A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land takes into account the weather conditions and forecasts for that land at the time of the application.

For the purposes of regulation 31(5): (a) the area of the holding excludes any land on which the occupier does not spread fertiliser or work the soil; and (b) the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure is to be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14.
A notice must inform the person of the effect of regulation 31.

In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, any reference to a numbered regulation or Schedule is a reference to the regulation in, or Schedule to, these Regulations bearing that number, and any reference in a regulation or Schedule to a numbered paragraph is a reference to the paragraph in that regulation or Schedule bearing that number.
In regulation 26, 'storage period' has the meaning given in regulation 25(7).
A report under paragraph (1) must be published by the last day of the six-month period beginning with the day on which the relevant period ends.

For the purposes of rule 22(2)(g) of the Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (General Regulatory Chamber) Rules 2009, the only grounds of appeal under regulation 6 are that the relevant holding (or any part of it) does not drain into water which the Secretary of State proposes to identify, or to continue to identify, as polluted or which has been similarly identified in Wales or Scotland.
The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes shall, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
No person may spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.
Regulation 19 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.
No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about the farm.
The occupier of a holding must maintain a record of the total size of the holding calculated in accordance with regulation 4(3).
A record required under paragraph 15 must be made by 1st March for the calendar year concerned.
These Regulations come into force on 1st May 2015.

In calculating the area of the holding for the purposes of ascertaining the amount of nitrogen permitted to be spread, no account is taken of surface waters, hardstanding, buildings, roads, or woodland unless that woodland is used for grazing.

An owner or occupier of a relevant holding who is sent a notice under regulation 5(3)(b) or 5(3A)(b) may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal against the proposals or designation referred to in the notice.

Where a silo has retaining walls, the retaining walls must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 15.6 of BS 5502: Part 22: 2003.
The occupier of a holding must, within one week of sowing a crop on which the occupier spreads or intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser, record the crop sown and the date of sowing.
No person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on tillage land during the period from 1 September to 15 January (inclusive).
A notice must be submitted to NRW by 31 March 2024, accompanied by the enhanced nutrient management plan for the qualifying grassland holding.

The Secretary of State must ensure that the public are consulted about proposals arising from the review, that relevant information (including information about the right to participate and the body to which comments may be submitted) is made available, and that the public are given an opportunity to express comments and opinions before decisions on plans and programmes are made.

In relation to livestock manure, the nitrogen content must be calculated either by using the standard table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of that Schedule.
The Secretary of State must from time to time carry out a review of these Regulations, in so far as the Secretary of State has not already done so under regulation 39.

Throughout the year concerned, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) must not exceed 100 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not applied to agricultural land within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole.
A notice under regulation 12(3) must give any information in P's possession which identifies or assists in identifying the person who committed the act or default.

A structure to which the circumstances at regulation 5(a) apply ceases to be an exempt structure if it is substantially reconstructed, unless in SEPA's opinion (notified in writing) the risks of pollution will be reduced by such works.

The steps specified in an enforcement notice may include a requirement to establish and implement a Farm Waste Management Plan in accordance with the code of practice approved under section 51(1) of the Control of Pollution Act 1974.
A temporary field site must not be located in any single position for more than 12 consecutive months.
The occupier must record the date of ploughing within one week of ploughing on the holding.
The risk map must show land drains (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), sites suitable for temporary field heaps if that storage method is to be used, and land that has a low run-off risk.
In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may use software approved by the Welsh Ministers as an alternative method.
A person must not spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on land during the closed period.
The fertilisation plan must record the type of crop.
These Regulations are enforced by Natural Resources Wales (NRW).
Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system which, before 1 March 1991, was being used for the purpose of making silage or storing slurry.

Subject to paragraph 9, a silo, its effluent tank and channels and any pipes must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, paragraph 7(a) for at least 20 years.
On determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers may direct SEPA to modify any requirement of the notice.
In all other cases (i.e. where a slurry storage tank's walls are not made of earth), the tank shall not be filled to a level which allows less than 300 millimetres of freeboard.
The occupier must ensure that sites where supplementary drinking for livestock are provided are not located within 10 metres of a watercourse on any land during the relevant period.

The works, precautions or other steps specified in a regulation 7 notice must be, in the opinion of the Agency, appropriate having regard to the requirements of these Regulations for reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.

SEPA may serve notice on any person who has custody or control of any relevant substance in circumstances where the Regulations apply, requiring that person to carry out works, take precautions, or take other steps specified in the notice that SEPA considers appropriate, having regard to the Regulations' requirements, for reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of inland or coastal waters arising from the custody or control of that substance.

Examples of reasonable precautions in relation to soil include: establishing crops early in autumn months and during dry conditions; planting headland rows and beds across the base of any sloping land; undersowing or sowing a cover crop to stabilise soil after harvest; breaking up compacted soil; and establishing grass buffer strips in valleys, along contours or slopes, field edges or gateways.

Subject to paragraph 9, a silo, its effluent tank, channels, and pipes must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, paragraph 7(a) for at least 20 years.
The occupier must, during the relevant period, record within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser the amount of phosphate spread (kg).

Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under these Regulations, and that offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or attributable to neglect on the part of a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate, that individual is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

If the occupier is found in breach of the derogation conditions after the application has been granted but before the calendar year to which the application relates, the Agency may, taking into account the seriousness of the breach, revoke the derogation by sending written notice to the applicant before the calendar year for which the derogation was granted.
Regulation 2 shall not apply where a person makes bulk bagged silage on a farm in bags that are made of 1000 gauge polyethylene or material of at least equivalent impermeability and durability.
Spreading fertiliser during the closed periods is permitted on the crops specified in the Table in Schedule 4, provided that the maximum rate in column 2 of that Table is not exceeded.
These Regulations come into force on 1st May 2015.
"Relevant water abstraction" includes the abstraction of water for use for manufacturing food or drink for human consumption.

A person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed period on a crop specified in the table in regulation 22(5) provided the rate of nitrogen specified in the second column of that table is not exceeded.
The accounts must record the total agricultural area of the holding, the area covered by each specified crop type, and the number and category of animals kept on the holding.
In regulation 14, 'the Fertiliser Manual' means the Fertiliser Manual RB209, 8th edition.

The bund and the base of the area must be designed and constructed so that they are of sufficient strength and structural integrity that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to remain impermeable to water and oil for at least 20 years.
Where an occupier intends to spread phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must, within one week of sowing a crop, record the date of sowing.
In the Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, Schedule 2 Part 2, paragraph 21 is substituted with new text as specified.
For the purposes of paragraph (6)(c), the panel may, in exceptional circumstances, convene an oral hearing at which the appellant and the Agency may appear.
"Water supply source" means inland freshwaters or ground waters from which a relevant water abstraction is made or licensed to be made.
An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must maintain a map of the holding ('a risk map') in accordance with regulation 11.

Spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed periods is permitted on crops specified in the Table in Schedule 4, provided that the maximum rate in column 2 of that Table is not exceeded.
A temporary field site must not be within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole, or within 10 metres of surface water or a land drain (other than a sealed impermeable pipe).

For the purposes of these Regulations, a reference to an EU Directive is to be read as if any reference in that Directive to one or more member States in a provision imposing an obligation or conferring a discretion were a reference to the authority responsible, immediately before exit day, for the United Kingdom's compliance with that obligation or able to exercise that discretion in respect of England.

This regulation applies, without prejudice to regulations 7 and 8, in relation to nitrogen spread in any twelve-month period as manufactured nitrogen fertiliser and as nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure, on grass grown to achieve a minimum protein content of 16% once harvested and dried.
No person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on grassland with sandy or shallow soil between 1 September and 31 December (inclusive).
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser within 2 metres of surface water.
Regulation 28 does not apply to a holding on which organic manure is spread only in a greenhouse.
The surface area of a temporary field site must be as small as reasonably practicable to minimise the leaching effect of rainfall.
The Secretary of State must prepare a report on the implementation of these Regulations for each relevant period.
An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must maintain a map of the holding ('a risk map') in accordance with regulation 11.

A slurry storage tank must have adequate storage capacity for the likely quantities of slurry produced from time to time on the farm, having regard to the proposed method of disposal (including likely rates and times of disposal) and the matters in sub-paragraph (3).

Following any subsequent review under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means a map published on the Agency's website that is marked with the prescribed identification text and specifies the period to which it relates.
If the Agency grants the application, it must designate the holding in question as a derogated holding for the calendar year to which the application relates.
Where a person uses equipment to spread slurry by broadcasting, the equipment must have a trajectory of less than 4 metres from the ground.
Before revising or adding to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones, the Secretary of State must publish the proposals to revise or add to the designation.

The occupier must prepare accounts for the calendar year to which the derogation relates and submit those accounts to the Agency by the following 30th April, in the form and manner published by the Agency.

The closed period for grassland with soil of a type specified in the first column of the table in paragraph (3) is the period beginning with the first date specified in relation to that soil type in the second column of the table and ending with the second date so specified.
If the panel allows an appeal under regulation 38, the Agency must designate the holding concerned as a derogated holding for the calendar year for which the application was made.

An area is designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone if it is an area of land that drains into polluted waters, contributes to the pollution of those waters, and is marked as such a zone on a relevant map.
These Regulations apply in relation to England only.
In order to comply with the duty under paragraph (1), the Secretary of State must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of the restrictions.

If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under regulation 6(2)(b), the Secretary of State, when acting under regulation 4(5), must treat the water concerned as water which should not be identified (or continue to be identified) as polluted, and must treat any holding (or part of any holding) draining into that water accordingly, regardless of whether the owner or occupier of that holding appealed.
Regulation 17 does not apply to land which is covered by a greenhouse.

A requirement for a silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or any other product to comply with a specified standard is satisfied by compliance with any relevant international standard recognised for use as a standard by any EEA State, or a technical specification or code of practice (whether mandatory or not) recognised for use as a standard by a public authority of any EEA State, in so far as it enables the pollution prevention objectives to be met in an equivalent manner.

The Agency may serve a notice ('regulation 7 notice') on a person who has custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil, or is responsible for the silo, slurry storage system or fuel oil storage tank, requiring that person to carry out works or take precautions or other steps specified in the notice.
On sandy or shallow soil, the closed period for spreading slurry or manure on tillage land runs from 1st August to the following 31st December.
Livestock manure (other than slurry and poultry manure) spread under regulation 14(2) must not be spread directly on to surface water.

Within one week of spreading organic manure, the occupier must record: (a) the area on which organic manure is spread; (b) the quantity spread; (c) the date or dates; (d) the methods of spreading; (e) the type of organic manure; (f) the total nitrogen content; and (g) the amount of nitrogen available to the crop.
The provisions of the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 relating to the sanctions listed in regulation 13(1) apply as if they were provisions of these Regulations.
Where the occupier of a holding has relied on advice from a FACTS adviser for any purpose under the Regulations, the occupier must keep a copy of that advice.

statements.statement_text: A land manager must ensure that organic manure or manufactured fertiliser is not applied to agricultural land if the soil is waterlogged, flooded or snow covered.

An occupier of a holding who keeps any of the animals specified in Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period, and all poultry manure produced in a yard or building on the holding during the storage period.
The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates.

No person having custody or control of any crop made into silage in the manner described in regulation 6(1) shall open or empty any bag in which silage has been made unless that person does so at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year using the Table in Schedule 1.

A person is regarded as having been found in breach of the derogation conditions where they have been convicted of an offence under regulation 41 arising from a breach of those conditions and either no further appeal may be made against the conviction or, where there was an appeal, it was decided against the person.
These Regulations apply in relation to England only.

The total amount of nitrogen permitted to be spread on any listed crop is the figure given in the permitted amount column, adjusted in accordance with the notes to the table and multiplied by the total area in hectares of that crop sown on the holding.

Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record, for the previous storage period, the number of animals in a building or hardstanding on the holding during that period and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system in relation to which construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was commenced before 1 March 1991, provided the work was completed before 1 September 1991.

Any other organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) applied onto the surface of bare soil or stubble must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest, where the land is within 50 metres of surface water and slopes such that there may be run-off to that water.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not applied to agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
For the purposes of calculating the area of the holding under paragraph (7), land on which the occupier does not spread fertiliser or work the soil is excluded from that area.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure exclusively in the form of certified compost applied to any given hectare does not exceed 1000 kg in any four year period, where it is applied as mulch to orchard land.

Livestock manure (other than slurry and poultry manure) may be spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as a species-rich semi-natural grassland that is notified as a Site of Special Scientific Interest under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
The fertilisation plan must record the optimum amount of nitrogen that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of nitrogen calculated under regulation 10(1)(a).
The standard total nitrogen content of cattle slurry is 2.6 kg per cubic metre for the purposes of calculating nitrogen in organic manure under Regulations 9, 36 and 37.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

For the purposes of regulation 28, nitrogen content must be ascertained either by using the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 2, or by sampling and analysis as set out in Part 2 of that Schedule.

The Secretary of State must ensure that the public are given an opportunity to express comments and opinions when all options are under consideration and before decisions on the plans and programmes are made.

The occupier of a holding, acting on the written advice of a FACTS adviser, may spread or permit the spreading of nitrogen in an amount so advised even if it exceeds the amount otherwise permitted for grass under regulation 12, subject to the maximum limits in paragraph (3).
