statements.statement_text: No later than the end of each four-year monitoring period, the Secretary of State must identify water affected by pollution (or at risk thereof), identify land draining into such waters, take into account unforeseen changes, and if necessary revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones.
No person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on grassland during the period from 15 September to 15 January (inclusive).

In the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016, Schedule 2, paragraph 17(2)(b), the reference to 'the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) Regulations 2013' is substituted with 'the Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021'.

A person who has custody or control of field silage or silage stored on open land must ensure the place is at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters, and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant water abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage effluent could enter if it escaped.

The fertilisation plan must be in permanent form and must record, in relation to the area planted or intended to be planted: the soil type; the previous crop (and if grass, whether managed by cutting or grazing); the amount of available soil nitrogen calculated and the method used; the expected planting month; the expected yield if arable; and the optimum amount of nitrogen to be spread.
The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any 12-month period, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure spread on any given hectare on the holding does not exceed 250 kg.
If the panel allows an appeal under regulation 38, the Agency must designate the holding concerned as a derogated holding for the calendar year for which the application was made.

A derogation granted under regulation 36 ceases to have effect unless the occupier to whom the derogation is granted has sent to the Agency a written declaration that the conditions set out in Schedule 3 (the derogation conditions) will be met in relation to the holding.
Within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier must record the date of spreading.
In regulation 16, 'regulatory provision' has the same meaning as in sections 28 to 32 of the 2015 Act (see section 32 of that Act).

When carrying out a review under paragraph (2), the Welsh Ministers must take into account available scientific and technical data, particularly with reference to respective nitrogen contributions originating from agricultural and other sources.
The Secretary of State must publish any guidance issued under regulation 15(1) on a website maintained by or on behalf of the Secretary of State.
A notice must specify or describe the works, precautions or other steps that the person is required to carry out or take.

A water supply source is a protected water supply source for the purposes of regulation 24(1)(c)(ii) if any relevant water abstraction from the source is licensed under Part 2 of the Water Resources Act 1991.

A person is regarded as having been found in breach of the derogation conditions where they have accepted a simple caution for an offence under regulation 41 arising from a breach of those conditions.
The amount of nitrogen produced by livestock must be calculated in accordance with Schedule 1.
The requirements of the regulations listed in Schedule 4 do not apply in relation to a new holding until the dates set out in Schedule 4.

An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record details of a contingency plan to be used in the event that an agreement for a person to accept the livestock manure fails.

No part of a slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions are taken that NRW agrees in writing are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
No person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with all other soils (not sandy or shallow) between 1 October and 31 January (inclusive).

Before determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers must, if requested by the appellant or SEPA, afford them an opportunity of appearing before and being heard by a person appointed by the Scottish Ministers for that purpose.
The occupier must, during the relevant period, record within one week of spreading organic manure the total phosphorus content (kg).
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of any of regulations 3 to 10 commits an offence.
In assessing whether it was reasonable for P to rely on information supplied by another person, particular regard must be had to whether P had any reason to disbelieve the information.
If circumstances change, the occupier must update the risk map within three months of the change.
Regulation 20 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser in a greenhouse.

A report published under regulation 16 must in particular: (a) set out the objectives intended to be achieved by the regulatory provision; (b) assess the extent to which those objectives are achieved; (c) assess whether those objectives remain appropriate; and (d) if those objectives remain appropriate, assess the extent to which they could be achieved in another way involving less onerous regulatory provision.

For the purposes of the nitrogen application limits in paragraphs (1) and (2), the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 9 for establishing nitrogen content.

All remaining provisions of the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010 are revoked in relation to all other holdings (not situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone) on 1 August 2024.
The occupier of a holding must, within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, record the amount of nitrogen spread.
Land comes within regulation 17(3) if it is subject to an agri-environmental commitment entered into under Council Regulation (EC) 1698/2005 or Regulation (EU) 1305/2013.
The results of soil sampling and analysis may have been collected before the date on which these Regulations come into force, including by another land manager.

A requirement for a silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or any other product to comply with a specified standard is satisfied by compliance with a technical specification or code of practice recognised for use as a standard by a public authority of any EEA State (whether mandatory or not), in so far as it enables the pollution prevention objectives of the Regulation to be met in an equivalent manner.
A heap of solid manure forming a temporary field site must occupy as small a surface area as is practically required to support the mass of the heap and prevent it from collapse.

For the purposes of regulation 24(1)(c)(ii), a water supply source is a protected water supply source if any relevant water abstraction from the source is licensed under Part 2 of the Water Resources Act 1991, or if the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the making of the silage began or, if the silage was made elsewhere, before it was stored on the land in question.
No other form of organic manure may be spread over the land in question during the applicable period provided for under paragraph (4)(a) or (b) (Condition 3).
Where the application is of livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure), the manure must not be applied directly onto the surface of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.
A report published under regulation 16 must set out the objectives intended to be achieved by the regulatory provision referred to in paragraph (1)(a).
The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure (tonnes or cubic metres as applicable) that is intended to be sent off the holding during the relevant period.
For a dairy cow after first calf, the daily manure produced is 64 litres, daily nitrogen is 315 grams and daily phosphate is 142 grams (first sub-category), as prescribed by Schedule 1.
For the purposes of regulation 13, the total amount of nitrogen from organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14 for establishing available nitrogen.
The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels, and reception pit must be impermeable.
The occupier must assess and record the amount of nitrogen (kg) in the livestock manure recorded under paragraph 18(1)(a), in accordance with regulation 36(4) and Parts 1 and 2 of Schedule 3.

A requirement for a silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or any other product to comply with a specified standard is satisfied by compliance with a relevant standard or code of practice of a national standards body or equivalent body of any EEA State.

Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow out of the channel is controlled by a sluice, the reception pit must have adequate capacity to hold the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
Each valve on a drainage pipe must be capable of shutting off the flow of slurry through the pipe, and must be kept shut and locked when not in use.

Where a storage area contains more than one fuel storage tank and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank within the area, or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil that could be stored in all tanks within the area.
A person guilty of an offence under regulation 41 is liable on summary conviction to a fine, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.
A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil is waterlogged, flooded, snow covered, or has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.
Schedule 2 applies for the purposes of calculating nitrogen in manure under Regulations 14(2), 14(4), 14(5), 27(3) and 28(4).

Where an appeal has been made against a regulation 30 notice, the compliance period is extended (subject to any direction under paragraph (5)) so that it expires on the date the Welsh Ministers finally determine the appeal, or, if the appeal is withdrawn, on the date of withdrawal.

Regulation 31 does not apply where, in any calendar year, (a) the requirements under regulation 31(5) are met, and (b) the occupier makes a record demonstrating that they are met. The requirements under regulation 31(5) are that throughout the year: (a) at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass; (b) total nitrogen in organic manure applied does not exceed 100 kg per hectare; (c) total nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser does not exceed 90 kg per hectare; and (d) the occupier does not bring organic manure onto the holding.

"Agri-environmental commitment" means any commitment entered into under Council Regulation (EC) No. 1698/2005 on support for rural development by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development or Regulation (EU) No. 1305/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on support for rural development by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development.
For the purposes of regulation 29, the 'storage period' for pigs and poultry is the period between 1 October and 1 April (all dates inclusive).
The permitted amount of nitrogen for grass is 300 kg per hectare (no standard yield applies).

The enhanced nutrient management plan for the holding must include a risk map produced in accordance with paragraph 11(1) indicating the location of the fields to which the plan relates, and must clearly state in relation to any field referred to in the plan the type of fertiliser to be used.
The total annual amount of livestock manure (other than slurry and poultry manure) spread under regulation 14(2) must not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.
Checking the organic matter content in, and moisture levels of, the soil is an example of a reasonable precaution for the purposes of compliance with regulation 4(3).

Livestock manure (other than slurry and poultry manure) may be spread within 10 metres of surface water where: it is spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or species-rich semi-natural grassland that is either a notified SSSI or subject to a qualifying agri-environment commitment; it is spread between 1 June and 31 October inclusive; it is not spread directly onto surface water; and the total annual amount does not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.

Throughout the year concerned, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) must not exceed 100 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
The plan must record the reference or name of the relevant field.

Before determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers must, if requested by the appellant or NRW, afford them an opportunity to appear before and be heard by a person appointed by the Welsh Ministers for that purpose.
When carrying out the review under paragraph (1)(a), the Secretary of State must take into account regional environmental conditions.

A notice under regulation 4B must include a written statement that the occupier intends during the relevant period to apply to the holding a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

In determining adequate storage capacity under sub-paragraphs (1) and (2), account must be taken of the storage capacity of any other slurry storage tank on the premises and the likely quantities of rainfall (including snow, hail or sleet) that may fall or drain into the slurry storage tank during the likely maximum storage period.

Examples of reasonable precautions in relation to livestock include: moving livestock regularly; erecting fencing around inland freshwaters or coastal waters; and wintering livestock on well-drained, level fields.
No person may spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water, unless using precision spreading equipment, in which case no person may spread organic manure within 6 metres of surface water.
These Regulations may be cited as the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015.
References to 'application' of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser do not include the direct deposit of excreta onto land by livestock.

The fertilisation plan for the holding must include a sketch plan indicating the location of the fields to which the plan relates, and must clearly state in relation to any field referred to in the plan the nature of the fertilizer to be used.
These Regulations are titled the Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021.
The five samples must be taken from a vessel; if reasonably practicable the slurry must be thoroughly mixed before sampling, and each sample must be taken from a different location.

For the purposes of regulation 5, 'cultivated agricultural land' means agricultural land which has been cultivated by physical means (including ploughing, sowing or harvesting) at least once in the previous year.

Where an occupier intends to spread slurry or poultry manure on land with a low run-off risk (making storage facilities otherwise unnecessary), storage facilities for an additional one week's manure must nonetheless be provided as a contingency measure in the event that spreading is not possible on some dates.

Where a sampling station has recorded nitrate concentration below 25 mg/l in all previous samples taken under the monitoring obligation and no new factor likely to increase nitrate content has appeared, the monitoring cycle is extended so that the first review falls before 1 January 2021 and recurs every eight years thereafter.

The occupier must ensure that the only livestock manure applied to the holding during the relevant period, whether directly by an animal or by spreading, is manure produced by the livestock on the holding.

An occupier of a holding who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must calculate the optimum amount of nitrogen that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the nitrogen available from the soil nitrogen supply.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil to be kept in a new or improved store must give the Agency notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location at least 14 days before work constructing the new or improved store is to be begun.
A closed period for ploughing grass applies on a holding subject to Schedule 1A enhanced nutrient management requirements.
The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the quantity of organic manure spread.
A land manager must ensure that poaching is prevented within 5 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.

For the purposes of regulation 3(1)(c)(ii), a water supply source is a protected water supply source if any relevant water abstraction from the source is licensed under Part II of the Water Resources Act 1991, or if the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the making of the silage began or, if the silage was made elsewhere, before it was stored on the land in question.
Schedule 3 sets out requirements for fuel oil storage areas pursuant to Regulation 5(1).
A person guilty of an offence under regulation 11 is liable, on summary conviction or on conviction on indictment, to a fine.

Where the size of a holding changes, the occupier of the holding must update the record required by regulation 35(1) of the old Regulations, or by regulation 25A of these Regulations, within one month.
If the size of the holding changes, the occupier must update the record of the total size of the holding within one month of that change.
An occupier who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must record the crop sown within one week of sowing that crop.
The base of a silo must extend beyond any walls of the silo.
The first report under regulation 40 must be published before 31 March 2020; subsequent reports must be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years.
No person may spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil is waterlogged, flooded, snow covered, frozen, or has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.
For the purposes of regulation 46, 'director', in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, means a member of the body corporate.
From the end of the closed period until the end of February, there must be at least three weeks between each spreading of slurry or poultry manure.

Before determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State must, if requested by the appellant or the Agency, afford them an opportunity of appearing before and being heard by a person appointed by the Secretary of State for the purpose.
Where any grass on the holding is ploughed, the land must be sown with grass within six weeks beginning with the day after the ploughing.

In the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016, Schedule 2, paragraph 17(2)(b), the reference to 'the Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) Regulations 2013' is substituted with 'the Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021'.

The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record: (a) the area spread, (b) the quantity of organic manure spread, (c) the date, (d) the method, (e) the type of organic manure, (f) the total nitrogen content, and (g) the amount of nitrogen available to the crop.
The base of a silo must have adequate provision for the drainage of silage effluent from the perimeter channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
A person having custody or control of slurry must store it in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2 or is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 5.
Poultry manure must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest.
An appeal under regulation 38 must be made in the form and manner published by the Secretary of State.
The land manager must ensure that reasonable precautions are taken to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from applications of slurry, manure or agricultural effluent.
In the Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, paragraph 21 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 is substituted as provided by WSI 2021/77 regulation 49(2)(a).
A person having custody or control of slurry must store it only in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2.
During the relevant period, the spreading of organic manure near surface water on a holding is subject to specific requirements under Schedule 1A.

Where a silo has a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more, the capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres.
Having carried out a review under paragraph (1), the Secretary of State must set out the conclusions in a report.
The nutrient management plan must be in permanent form.
The occupier may establish the total amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3.

The 5-year record retention obligation in regulation 35(1) applies equally to records required to be made under the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008 in relation to which regulation 45 of those Regulations had effect immediately before the commencement of these Regulations.
A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must not be filled to a level that allows less than 750 millimetres of freeboard.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in a fuel storage tank within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any year beginning 1 January, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
The requirement in paragraph (1) shall not apply where the total quantity of fuel oil stored on the farm does not exceed 1,250 litres.
These Regulations may be cited as the Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 2003 and shall come into force on 1st December 2003.
Solid manure may be stored on a temporary field site only if it can be stacked in a free-standing heap and does not drain liquid from the material.
A person who applies organic manure on to the surface of bare soil or stubble (other than soil that has been sown) must ensure that it is incorporated into the soil in accordance with regulation 19.

Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate (or any combination) may be spread within 10 metres of surface water but not within 6 metres of surface water, provided the spreading equipment used is a trailing hose band spreader, a trailing shoe band spreader, an injector injecting no deeper than 10 cm below the soil surface, or a dribble bar applicator.
Regulation 32 applies to any silo or slurry storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 28 April 2021.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any year beginning 1 January, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

A requirement for a silo or slurry storage tank to conform to a British Standard is satisfied if the silo or tank conforms to a standard or specification that provides an equivalent level of protection and performance.

A person who contravenes regulation 5(1) of the Regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.

A person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil during the period beginning 1st August and ending the following 15th September, provided the next crop sown on the land is sown on or before 15th September.

If any part of an effluent tank is below ground level, the tank must be designed and constructed so that it is likely to continue to satisfy the structural integrity and impermeability requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 for at least 20 years without maintenance.

SEPA may serve notice on any person who has custody or control of any relevant substance in circumstances where the Regulations apply, requiring that person to carry out works, take precautions or take other steps specified in the notice that SEPA considers appropriate to reduce to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of inland or coastal waters.

Regulation 25 (storage capacity) does not apply in relation to a new holding until 31st July in the third calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include the new holding.
No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in drums within a storage area in relation to which the requirements of Schedule 3 are satisfied.

Regulation 24 (separation of slurry) does not apply in relation to a new holding until 31st July in the third calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include the new holding.

Regulation 18 (restrictions on spreading slurry) does not apply in relation to a new holding until 31st July in the third calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include the new holding.

A person who has custody or control of field silage or silage stored on open land must give the Agency notice of the place where the silage is to be made or stored at least 14 days before the place is first used for that purpose.
The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.

The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the type of organic manure, the total nitrogen content, and the amount of nitrogen that was available to the crop.

An occupier of a holding who has submitted an undertaking to the organic farming control system under Article 27 of Council Regulation (EC) 834/2007 may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen at any time on crops listed in Schedule 4 (permitted crops for the closed period).
At the same time as serving a notice of appeal on the Scottish Ministers, the appellant must send a copy of the notice and any accompanying statement to SEPA.
The occupier must produce an enhanced nutrient management plan for the spreading of phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period.
For the purposes of regulation 46, 'director', in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, means a member of the body corporate.
An application relating to the calendar year commencing on 1st January 2017 may be submitted by 20th March 2017.
The derogation conditions set out in Schedule 3 apply for the purposes of Regulation 36(4).
The occupier must make a record of the calculations and how the final figures were arrived at.
Schedule 4 sets out transitional dates applicable to new holdings for the purposes of Regulation 5A.

A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land is planned so that it does not give rise to a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.

The occupier of a holding who has submitted an undertaking to the organic control system under Article 27 of Council Regulation (EC) 834/2007 may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen during a closed period on winter oilseed rape, asparagus, brassica, grass, over-wintered salad onions, parsley, bulb onions, or on any other crop in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser.
