statements.statement_text: The occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen in the livestock manure recorded under paragraph 15(1)(a), in accordance with Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 2.
For the purposes of Regulation 32, 'construction' includes substantial enlargement and reconstruction.
The panel appointed under regulation 38 must consist of an odd number of persons and must consist of at least 3 persons.
The fertilisation plan must record the previous crop and, if it was grass, whether it was managed by cutting or grazing.

The Welsh Ministers must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of the measures imposed by the Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution from agricultural sources.
Solid poultry manure that does not have bedding mixed into it and is stored on a temporary field site must be covered with an impermeable material.

The occupier of a holding with livestock must maintain a record of the amount of storage capacity (slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 29, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported, the amount intended to be spread on low run-off risk land, and (for slurry vessels) the amount of liquid other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.

Where the occupier of a holding introduces animals on to the holding for the first time, the occupier must, within one month of that introduction, calculate and record the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding, the amount of manure intended to be spread on land with a low run-off risk, and, in the case of a slurry vessel, the amount of liquids other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.
The first report under regulation 16 must be published before 2nd April 2021.
For a veal calf, the daily manure produced is 7 litres, daily nitrogen is 23 grams and daily phosphate is 12.7 grams, as prescribed by Schedule 1.
All nitrogen content of livestock manure must be ascertained using either the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 3 or by sampling and analysis as set out in Part 2 of that Schedule.

Where a silo has retaining walls, those walls must be capable of withstanding minimum wall loadings calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 15.6 of BS 5502: Part 22:2003.

A requirement for a silo, slurry storage system, fuel storage tank or any other product to comply with a specified standard is satisfied by compliance with any relevant international standard recognised for use as a standard by any EEA State, in so far as it enables the pollution prevention objectives of the Regulation to be met in an equivalent manner.
The occupier must, during the relevant period, record within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser the date of spreading.
"Relevant water abstraction" includes the abstraction of water for use for domestic purposes (within the meaning given by section 218 of the Water Industry Act 1991) other than human consumption.
Regulation 30 does not apply to a crop growing in a greenhouse.

The occupier of a holding with livestock must maintain a record of the amount of manure that will be produced by the anticipated number of animals kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period referred to in regulation 29, using the figures in Schedule 1.
Within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier must record: (a) the date of spreading; and (b) the amount of nitrogen spread.

A water supply source is a protected water supply source if the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the silage was stored on the land in question, where the silage was made elsewhere.

The restriction in paragraph (1) applies only if each hectare on which the organic manure is spread does not receive more than 150 kg total nitrogen between the start of the applicable closed period under regulation 20 and the end of the following February.

The occupier of a holding must not store organic manure (other than slurry), or bedding contaminated with organic manure, except in a vessel, in a covered building, on an impermeable surface, or (for solid manure that can be stacked in a free-standing heap and does not drain liquid) on a temporary field site.
A temporary field site must not be located in any single position for more than 12 consecutive months.
The Secretary of State must from time to time publish a report setting out the conclusions of the review.

The base and walls of the slurry storage tank, any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.

A structure to which the circumstances at regulation 5(a) apply ceases to be an exempt structure if any requirement of a notice under regulation 8(1) is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.

Where P relies on a third party allegation, the notice must identify or assist in identifying the person who committed the act or default or supplied the information relied on, and must be served on the person bringing the proceedings not less than 7 clear days before the hearing.
Where a silo has retaining walls made other than of earth, the base of the silo must extend beyond those retaining walls.
If the amount of storage capacity changes, the occupier must record the change within one week.

In the case of brassica, an additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the applicable closed period up to the date of harvest, provided this does not cause the total to exceed the 150 kg per hectare limit imposed by regulation 21(2).

Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on the premises in any two-day period (disregarding slurry transferred directly into a slurry storage tank).

Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must have adequate provision for the drainage of slurry from the collection channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to dismiss the appeal.

Regulations 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 23, 25A, 25B, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, and 34 do not apply in relation to a new holding until the beginning of the second calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include that new holding.
A person (P) may not rely on a due diligence defence involving a third party allegation unless P has either served the required notice or obtained the leave of the court.
Throughout the year concerned, at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area must be sown with grass.
No person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on grassland during the period from 15 September to 15 January (inclusive).
Before the relevant date every year, the occupier must make a record of the number and category of animals on the holding during the previous 12-month period.

The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010 are revoked in relation to a holding or part of a holding situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone (as shown on the Nitrate Vulnerable Zones Index Map 2013) on 1 April 2021.

No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must identify water that is affected by pollution, or could be if the controls in these Regulations are not applied in the area concerned, using the criteria in Annex I to Council Directive 91/676/EEC.
These Regulations may be cited as the Reduction and Prevention of Agricultural Diffuse Pollution (England) Regulations 2018.

The slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.
In relation to slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, at least five samples, each of 2 litres, must be taken.

Where the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones before 1st January 2017, the Secretary of State must, by 1st March 2017, send written notice to any person appearing to the Secretary of State to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.

Where the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones before 1st January 2017, the Secretary of State must, by 31st December 2016, publish the proposals to revise or add to the designation on the Agency's website.
An appeal under regulation 9 must be made by the appellant serving notice on the Scottish Ministers, and the notice must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal.

If the occupier is found in breach of the derogation conditions after the application has been granted but before the calendar year to which the application relates, the Agency may revoke the derogation by sending written notice to the applicant before that calendar year, taking into account the seriousness of the breach.
A slurry storage system must satisfy the requirements set out in Schedule 6.

A sow (including her litters up to a weight of 7 kg per piglet) fed on a diet without synthetic amino acids is attributed daily production of 10.9 litres of manure, 49 grams of nitrogen and 37 grams of phosphate.
No part of a fuel oil storage area or its enclosing bund shall be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which fuel oil could enter if it were to escape.

The closed period for tillage land with soil of a type specified in the first column of the table in paragraph (3) is the period beginning with the first date specified in relation to that soil type in the third column of the table and ending with the second date so specified, subject to paragraph (4).

A 'relevant holding' means land and any associated buildings at the disposal of the occupier which are used for growing crops in soil or rearing livestock for agricultural purposes, and which are wholly or partly in an area which the Secretary of State has proposed should be, or should continue to be, designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone, or which the Secretary of State has so designated.
The prohibition in paragraph (1) does not apply to silage while it is stored temporarily in a container, trailer or vehicle in connection with its transport about the farm or elsewhere.
On determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers may direct NRW to dismiss the appeal.
A silo or slurry storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 28 April 2021 is defined as 'a new or improved store' for the purposes of Regulation 32.
The prohibition in paragraph (1) does not apply to silage while it is stored temporarily in a container, trailer or vehicle in connection with its transport about the farm or elsewhere.
Before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must record the amount required.
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading organic manure, the amount of phosphate that was supplied for uptake by the crop.
Adequate provision must be made for the drainage of silage effluent from the collection channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
Where fuel from a tank is discharged through a flexible pipe permanently attached to the tank, the pipe shall be kept locked in a way which ensures that it is kept within the bund when not in use.

Any reference to the period stated in a regulation 7 notice is to that period as extended if it has been extended under regulation 7(5)(b) or by virtue of regulation 8(6); and any reference to a requirement of a notice is to that requirement as modified if it has been modified under regulation 7(5).
The risk map must show each field marked with a reference number or number to enable cross-reference to fields recorded in fertilisation plans.
The bund and the base of the area must be impermeable to water and oil.
For the purposes of regulation 29, the 'storage period' means: (a) 1 October to 1 April (inclusive) for pigs and poultry; and (b) 1 October to 1 March (inclusive) in any other case.
For the purposes of regulation 7, the amount of nitrogen is to be calculated in accordance with Schedule 1.
In Part 1, references to 'pollution' in relation to water must be construed in accordance with regulation 4(5)(a).
A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser on land if there is a significant risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.
The 2001 Regulations are revoked.
The occupier must ensure that during the relevant period no person spreads organic manure within 15 metres of surface water.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure exclusively in the form of certified compost does not exceed 1000 kg per hectare in any four-year period when applied as mulch to orchard land, or 500 kg per hectare in any two-year period when applied to any other land.

The occupier of a holding with livestock must maintain a record of the amount of manure that will be produced by the anticipated number of animals kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period referred to in regulation 29, using the figures in Schedule 1.

Where phosphorus soil sampling analysis of the agricultural area of the holding with the same cropping regime, nutrient management regime and soil type has not been carried out within the period beginning with 1 January 2020 and ending with 31 December 2023, such sampling analysis must be undertaken within the period beginning with 1 January 2024 and ending with 30 March 2024.
The notice and accompanying enhanced nutrient management plan must be submitted to NRW by e-mail.

In regulation 13(5), 'representative autumn soil samples' means soil samples taken during the period beginning with 1st September and ending with the following 31st October which provide a representative indication of mineral nitrogen levels in the soil on which the relevant grass is grown, taking into account the number of fields, soil type and terrain.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in a fuel storage tank within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.

No person may spread nitrogen fertiliser on land if there is a significant risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, having regard in particular to the slope of the land (especially if more than 12°), ground cover, proximity to surface water, weather conditions, soil type, and the presence of land drains.

Having carried out consultation under this regulation, the Secretary of State must inform the public about the considerations upon which those decisions are based, including the participation by the public.
In deciding whether to revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones, the Secretary of State must have regard to the recommendations made under paragraph (1).
The occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure for the purposes of regulation 8 by using the table in Part 1 of Schedule 3.

Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 100% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the date on which a derogation is next granted to the occupier.

For the purposes of regulation 5, 'cultivated agricultural land' means agricultural land which has been cultivated by chemical means (including the application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser) at least once in the previous 3 years.

In relation to livestock manure, the nitrogen content must be calculated either by using the standard table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of that Schedule.
If circumstances change, the occupier must update the risk map within three months of the change.

Livestock manure (other than slurry and poultry manure) may be spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as a species-rich semi-natural grassland that is subject to an agri-environment commitment entered into under Council Regulation (EC) 1698/2005 or Regulation (EU) 1305/2013.

Where all fuel oil in the storage area is contained in more than one tank, the bund must be capable of retaining the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank, or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil that could be stored in all tanks within the area.
A reference to a slurry storage system includes a slurry storage tank and any reception pit and any effluent tank used in connection with the tank.

The occupier must make a record of the nitrogen calculations and how the final figures were arrived at; where the occupier uses software approved by the Secretary of State, the occupier must keep a printout of the result.
The permitted amount of nitrogen for field beans is 0 kg per hectare, and for peas is 0 kg per hectare, meaning no nitrogen may be spread on those crops.
A notice under regulation 4B must include the name of the occupier of the qualifying grassland holding.

Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must ascertain it as soon as reasonably practicable after arrival and record it within one week of ascertaining it.

Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop concerned during the growing season.

Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under these Regulations committed with the consent, connivance, or attributable to neglect of a director, manager, secretary, or similar officer (or person purporting to act in such capacity), that individual is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly; but this does not apply to contraventions under regulations 24(1), 24(4), 25(1), 30(5) or 32.
A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain a summary of the monitoring results obtained by the Agency under regulation 4.

The base of a silo must be constructed using appropriate hot-rolled asphalt in accordance with BS 5502:Part 21:1990 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for selection and use of construction materials).
Application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser includes mixing with the surface layers of the soil.
A person who contravenes regulation 9 is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale.

The occupier must protect all soil by ensuring that all land is covered by crops, stubbles, residues or other vegetation at all times, except where establishing such cover would create a significant risk of soil erosion and significant risk of nitrogen and phosphorus getting into surface water.

The Secretary of State must, before 1 January 2017 and before 1 January of every fourth year thereafter, monitor the nitrate concentration in freshwaters over a period of one year at sampling stations representative of surface water (at least monthly and more frequently during flood periods) and at sampling stations representative of groundwater (at regular intervals).

Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under regulation 41, and the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or attributable to neglect on the part of, a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer (or a person purporting to act in such a capacity), that individual is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

In relation to an offence under regulation 11(1), the Agency may impose a restoration notice, compliance notice, stop notice, fixed monetary penalty, variable monetary penalty, or accept an enforcement undertaking, as if it were an offence specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.

These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which was not used before 1st March 1991 for the relevant purpose but was constructed before that date for such use.
These Regulations shall extend to Scotland only.
For poultry manure, the available nitrogen for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread is 30% (applicable on and after 1st January 2014).
The prohibition in paragraph (1) does not apply to a holding on which organic manure is spread only in a greenhouse.
No person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil between 1 August and 31 December (inclusive).

When planning the application of agricultural diffuse pollution sources, the land manager must ensure that the soil type and condition of the land is taken into account as a factor indicating significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
'Liquid digested sewage sludge' means liquid from the treatment of sewage sludge by anaerobic digestion.
The factors relevant to the significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution in regulation 9(2) include those set out in regulation 4(2).
In the case of grass, a maximum of 40kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time.
In all cases, the base of the silo must be provided with channels constructed so as to collect any silage effluent which may escape from the silo.

The only ground of appeal under regulation 6 is that the relevant holding (or any part of it) drains into water which the Secretary of State should not identify, or should not continue to identify, as polluted.

Where the size of a holding changes (in respect of land not covered by a greenhouse), the occupier must update the record required by regulation 35(1) of the old Regulations or regulation 25A of these Regulations within one month.
SEPA may at any time extend the period for compliance with any requirement of a notice served under regulation 8.
The base of a silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes shall be impermeable.
Every part of any fuel storage tank must be situated within the bund.
Application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser does not include the direct deposit of excreta onto land by livestock.

Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate (or any combination) may be spread using a trailing hose band spreader or a trailing shoe band spreader, except within 6 metres of surface water.

An occupier of a holding who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must calculate the soil nitrogen supply, calculate the optimum amount of nitrogen to be spread, and produce a spreading plan for that growing season.

Whether taken from a vessel or during spreading, the five samples must be poured into a larger container, stirred thoroughly, and a 2-litre sample taken from that container into a smaller clean container; that 2-litre composite sample must then be sent for analysis.

The effluent collection system associated with silos may, with the agreement of SEPA, incorporate a system of pumps and sumps together with detailed sizing, pumping and management requirements, designed to reduce the capacity of the effluent tank.
A person who contravenes regulation 9 is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale.
A reference to a slurry storage system in these Regulations also includes any channels and pipes used in connection with the tank, any reception pit, or any effluent tank.

A person who contravenes regulation 7(4A) of the Regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.
Dirty water has a standard total nitrogen content of 0.5 kg per cubic metre for the purposes of calculating nitrogen in organic manure under Regulations 9, 36 and 37.

An occupier of a holding who stores any bedding contaminated with organic manure must store it in a vessel, in a covered building, on an impermeable surface, or (for qualifying solid manure) on a temporary field site.
Where the application is of livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure), the manure must be applied in the period beginning on 1st June and ending on 31st October.
These Regulations may be cited as the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015.

Any organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable, and within 24 hours at the latest, where the land is within 50 metres of surface water and slopes such that there may be run-off to that water.
An occupier who introduces animals onto a holding for the first time must comply with the record-keeping requirements of regulation 34(1) within one month of the introduction of the animals.
NRW may at any time withdraw a notice served under this regulation.
On determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers may direct NRW to withdraw the regulation 30 notice.
In the case of slurry and other liquid and semi-liquid organic manure, at least five samples, each of two litres, must be taken.
For grass, the maximum nitrogen application rate during the closed period is 80 kg/hectare.

As part of the review under regulation 39, the Secretary of State must review the overall position of derogations granted under this regulation against the objective of reducing water pollution caused or induced by nitrates from agricultural sources.

A reference in these Regulations to 'polluted water' includes freshwater that contains a concentration of nitrates greater than 50 mg/l, or that could do so if these Regulations were not to apply there.

The Welsh Ministers must review the effectiveness of the measures imposed by these Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution from agricultural sources at least every four years, and if necessary revise them.
A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain a summary of the most recent review conducted under regulation 39.
Each party to an appeal under regulation 38 must bear its own costs.
The requirement to have a compliant slurry storage system does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.
The Secretary of State must publish any guidance issued under regulation 15(1) on a website maintained by or on behalf of the Secretary of State.

Where land has been harvested using a combine harvester, forage harvester or mower, the occupier may alternatively satisfy the post-harvest obligation by preparing the land as a seedbed for a crop or temporary cover crop within 14 days of harvest and sowing the crop or temporary cover crop within 10 days beginning the day after final seedbed preparation.
The land manager must ensure that reasonable precautions are taken to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from land management and cultivation practices on agricultural land.
The risk map for the holding must show each field marked with a reference number or number to enable cross-reference to fields recorded in the fertilisation plan.

Spreading equipment with a spreading trajectory of more than 4 metres from the ground may be used on land that has a low run-off risk where such equipment can achieve an average slurry application rate of not more than 2 mm per hour when operating continuously.

An occupier of a holding who keeps any animals specified in column 1 of Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period and for all poultry manure produced in a yard or building on the holding during the storage period.

For the period beginning with 1st December 2016 and ending with the day on which the Secretary of State next revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means a map marked 'Nitrate Vulnerable Zones (England) 2017 to 2020' published on 1st December 2016 on the Agency's website.

The Agency may serve a notice on a person who has custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil, or is responsible for the silo, slurry storage system or fuel oil storage tank, requiring that person to carry out works or take precautions or other steps specified in the notice.

These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which, where not used before 1st March 1991, was constructed before that date for such use; or in relation to which a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1st March 1991, or such work was commenced before that date, provided the work was completed before 1st September 1991.

The Secretary of State must ensure that the public are consulted about the proposals in light of the review and that relevant information about such proposals is made available to the public, including information about the right to participate in decision-making and about the body to which comments or questions may be submitted.

'Certified compost' means green compost or green/food compost in relation to which the supplier confirms in writing that it meets the standards set out in PAS 100:2011 on composted materials dated January 2011 and contains no livestock manure; and the occupier must retain written confirmation that the organic manure complies with that definition.

The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage and Slurry) (Wales) Regulations 2010, regulations 3 and 9, are revoked in relation to all other holdings (not situated in a nitrate vulnerable zone) on 1 April 2021.
These Regulations may be cited as the Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Scotland) Regulations 2003 and shall come into force on 1st December 2003.
The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.
Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must record it within one week of ascertaining it.

A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser on land if there is a significant risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, with account taken in particular of: slope of the land (especially if greater than 12 degrees); ground cover; proximity to surface water; weather conditions; soil type; and presence of land drains.
Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate (or any combination) may be spread using a dribble bar applicator, except within 6 metres of surface water.
An occupier who brings livestock manure on to a holding must, within one week, record the type and amount of livestock manure.
Where fuel from a tank is discharged through a flexible pipe permanently attached to the tank, the pipe shall be fitted with a tap or valve at its end which closes automatically when not in use.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure exclusively in the form of certified compost applied to any given hectare does not exceed 500 kg in any two year period, where it is applied to any land other than orchard land.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure or manufactured fertiliser is not applied to agricultural land if the soil has been frozen for more than 12 hours in the previous 24 hours.

The Agency must, before 10th August 2016 and before 10th August of every fourth year thereafter, make recommendations to the Secretary of State as to which areas of land should be, or should continue to be, designated as nitrate vulnerable zones.
Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must produce a fertilisation plan for the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser for that growing season.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the total phosphate content of the organic manure.
The permitted amount of nitrogen for autumn or early winter sown wheat is 220 kg, based on a standard yield of 8.0 tonnes per hectare.
The base of a silo must be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must on each occasion calculate the amount of nitrogen from that manure that is likely to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
NRW must withdraw the notice, extend the period for compliance, or modify the requirements of the notice if so directed by the Welsh Ministers under regulation 31(5).
The requirement in paragraph (1) does not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.

Where samples are collected to calculate compliance with the whole farm limit for pigs and poultry, four samples for analysis must be taken in a calendar year (one per quarter) from manure heaps not more than 12 months old.

A derogation granted under regulation 36 ceases to have effect unless the occupier sends to the Agency a written declaration that the derogation conditions in Schedule 3 will be met, and that declaration must be sent within 28 calendar days of the derogation being granted.
On determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers may direct NRW to extend the period for compliance with any requirement of the regulation 30 notice.
The total nitrogen content of cattle slurry is 2.6 kg per cubic metre, as specified in the standard table for calculating nitrogen in manure.
The recording obligations in paragraph 20 are in addition to the requirements of regulation 40 (records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser).
The occupier must, within one week of sowing a crop on which the occupier spreads or intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser, record the crop sown and the date of sowing.
The fertilisation plan must record the reference or name of the relevant field.

Where the Agency grants an application in a case within paragraph (8) or decides not to revoke a derogation in a case within paragraph (9), it must refuse the next application made under regulation 36 by or on behalf of the occupier.
The walls of any pipes associated with slurry or effluent storage must be impermeable.
A silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank or container ceases to be an exempt structure if it ceases to be an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 7(1).
A slurry storage system must satisfy the requirements set out in Schedule 6.
"Relevant water abstraction" includes the abstraction of water for use for manufacturing food or drink for human consumption.
Any person who contravenes any provision of these Regulations (other than regulation 32) is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction, or on conviction on indictment, to a fine.
The base of a silo must have adequate provision for the drainage of silage effluent from the perimeter channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.

These Regulations apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank otherwise meeting the paragraph (1) exemption if any requirement of a notice under regulation 7 is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.

At least every four years, the Secretary of State must review the effectiveness of the restrictions in nitrate vulnerable zones imposed by these Regulations as a means of reducing or preventing water pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources.
The plan must record the area of the field planted or intended to be planted.
Slurry or liquid from the treatment of sewage sludge by anaerobic digestion must be incorporated into the soil as soon as practicable, and within 24 hours at the latest, after application.
Where any grass on the holding is ploughed during the relevant period, the land must be sown with grass within six weeks beginning with the day after the date of ploughing grass.

Where silage is a crop being made into field silage or is being stored on open land, the person with custody or control must give the Agency at least 14 days' notice before first using the place, and the place must be at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage effluent could enter if it escaped.

A temporary field site must not be in a field liable to flooding or becoming waterlogged, within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole or within 10 metres of surface water or a land drain (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), located in any single position for more than 12 consecutive months, located in the same place as an earlier one constructed within the last two years, or on land having a slope of 12 degrees or more which is within 30 metres of surface water.
No person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser within 2 metres of surface water.
These Regulations come into force on 2nd April 2018.
The Secretary of State may issue guidance to the Agency with respect to the exercise of the Agency's functions under these Regulations.
For the purposes of paragraph (3), 'officer' also means a person purporting to act in any such capacity.
A person who contravenes regulation 2(1), 2(2), 3(1), 4(1), 6 or 10 shall be guilty of an offence.

For grassland, the maximum phosphate application rates (kg P₂O₅/ha) by soil phosphorus index are: at grass establishment — 120 (index 0), 80 (1), 50 (2), 30 (3), 0 (4+); grazing — 80 (0), 50 (1), 20 (2), 0 (3), 0 (4+); hay — 80 (0), 55 (1), 30 (2), 0 (3), 0 (4+); silage first cut — 100 (0), 70 (1), 40 (2), 20 (3), 0 (4+); second cut — 25 (0–3), 0 (4+); third cut — 15 (0–3), 0 (4+); fourth cut — 10 (0–3), 0 (4+).
The period for compliance stated in a notice must be either 28 days or such longer period as is reasonable in the circumstances.
Any person using sampling and analysis to determine nitrogen content in organic manure must keep the original report from the laboratory.

Where no value is established for an organic manure for the purposes of the provisions referred to in regulation 14(1), the occupier may not spread that manure in reliance on those provisions on a crop referred to in regulation 12 or 13.
In the Conservation of Habitats and Species (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, regulation 104, paragraph (1)(b) and the word 'or' before it are omitted.
A report under regulation 40(2)(a) must set out the objectives intended to be achieved by these Regulations.
The occupier of a holding with livestock must also record the sites used for field heaps and the dates of use.
A notice of appeal must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal.
The Agency must withdraw the notice, extend the period for compliance, or modify the requirements of the notice if so directed by the Secretary of State under regulation 8(5).

In addition to planning obligations, a land manager must ensure that reasonable precautions are taken to prevent agricultural diffuse pollution resulting from applications, including checking spreading equipment for leaks and correct calibration, incorporating organic manure and manufactured fertiliser into the soil within 12 hours of or as soon as possible after application, and checking the organic matter content and moisture levels of the soil.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the amount of nitrogen likely to be available from the manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
A person who has custody or control of silage being made or stored must ensure the silage is kept in a silo that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 5.
Each sub-sample of solid manure must be taken at least 0.5 metres from the surface of the heap.
The volume of manure produced by animals on a holding must be calculated using the figures specified for daily manure produced by each animal in column 2 of Schedule 1.
Condition 1 is satisfied where organic manure is in the form of certified green compost or certified green/food compost.

The slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit shall be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for a period of at least 20 years.
On all other soils, the closed period for spreading slurry or manure on grassland runs from 15th October to the following 31st January.
The closed period for grassland is the period beginning 15th September and ending the following 15th January.

A slurry storage tank must have adequate storage capacity for the likely quantities of slurry produced from time to time on the premises, taking into account the proposed method of utilising the slurry, the likely rates and times of utilisation, and the matters in sub-paragraph (3).
The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
The Secretary of State must monitor the nitrate concentration in freshwaters over a period of one year before 1st January 2017 and before 1st January of every fourth year thereafter.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record the name and address of the recipient.

Where an occupier spreads organic manure using precision spreading equipment up to 6 metres from surface water as permitted by regulation 14(1), the risk map must identify land within 6 metres of surface waters; and the occupier must keep a copy of the risk map.
A dairy cow after her first calf with an annual milk yield of more than 9,000 litres is attributed daily production of 64 litres of manure, 315 grams of nitrogen and 142 grams of phosphate.
Before spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier must record the amount required.

If proposals for an alternative suite of measures for delivering the outcomes in regulation 44(1) are received within 18 months of these Regulations coming into force, the Welsh Ministers must consider whether those measures would deliver the outcomes more effectively than the measures contained in these Regulations.

At least every four years, the occupier of a derogated holding must undertake soil sampling and analysis for the supply of phosphorus of at least every five hectares of the agricultural area under the same cropping regime and soil type.
The occupier must make a record of the calculations and how the final figures were arrived at.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system which, where it was not used before 1 March 1991 for making silage or storing slurry, was constructed before that date for such use.
For the purposes of regulation 10(5), 'land management and cultivation practices' includes establishing seedbeds, polytunnels or tramlines.
The requirement in paragraph (1) does not apply where the total quantity of fuel oil stored on the farm does not exceed 1,500 litres.
A notice under regulation 4B must include the name of the occupier of the qualifying grassland holding.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel oil tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be shut and locked in the shut position when not in use.
Where an occupier intends to spread phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must, within one week of sowing a crop, record the crop sown.
The requirement in paragraph (1) does not apply to the temporary storage of fuel oil in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about a farm.
From the end of the closed period until the end of February, the maximum amount of slurry that may be spread at any one time is 30 cubic metres per hectare.
The permitted amount of nitrogen for winter oilseed rape is 250 kg, based on a standard yield of 3.5 tonnes per hectare.
Regulation 12 is subject to regulation 13 and applies irrespective of the figure given in the fertilisation plan.

An appeal under regulation 9 must be made by the appellant serving notice on the Scottish Ministers, and that notice must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the grounds of appeal; at the same time, the appellant must send a copy of the notice and any accompanying statement to SEPA.
A person having custody or control of slurry must store it in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2 or is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 5.
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, adequate provision shall be made for the drainage of slurry from the collection channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.

Subject to regulation 6, no person shall have custody or control of any crop being made into silage or any silage being stored unless it is compressed into bales that are wrapped and sealed within impermeable membranes (or enclosed in impermeable bags) and stored at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
Subsequent reports must be published at intervals not exceeding 5 years.
The occupier must ensure that no person ploughs temporary grassland on sandy soils on the holding within the period beginning with 1 July 2024 and ending with 31 December 2024.
A reference to a slurry storage system includes any channels and pipes used in connection with the tank, any reception pit, or any effluent tank.
A reference in these Regulations to 'polluted water' includes water that is eutrophic, or that may in the near future become eutrophic if these Regulations were not to apply there.

Where slurry is to be disposed of by spreading on land, the storage tank is not required to have a greater capacity than is adequate to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced in any continuous six-month period, having regard to the matters in sub-paragraph (3).
The base of a slurry storage tank must be impermeable.
A person having custody or control of slurry must have a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 6, and the slurry must be stored in that system.

The reference to a record required to be made under these Regulations includes a reference to a record required to be made under the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008 in relation to which regulation 45 of those Regulations had effect immediately before the commencement of these Regulations.

The dual-valve requirement in paragraph 10(1) does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank of equal or greater capacity, or where the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
Regulation 31 does not apply where, in any calendar year, the requirements under paragraph (5) are met and the occupier makes a record demonstrating that they are met.
Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February, there must be at least three weeks between any spreading of slurry or poultry manure.
Throughout the year concerned, at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area must be sown with grass.

For agricultural land to which the storage prohibition in regulation 9(1) does not apply, the land manager must ensure that any factors which mean there would be a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution are taken into account when deciding where to store organic manure.
No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored temporarily in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about the farm.
The Agency must determine an application under regulation 36 as soon as practicable.

A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land is planned so that it does not exceed the needs of the soil and crop on that land, and does not give rise to a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.

Regulation 14 sets out the method for calculating the amount of nitrogen in organic manure that is available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread (available nitrogen) for the purposes of regulations 8(9), 12(2), 13(4) and 31(6).

No person having custody or control of any crop being made or already made into silage in the manner described in regulation 2(1)(b) shall open or remove the wrapping of any bales unless that person does so at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.

When carrying out a review under regulation 44(2), the Welsh Ministers must take into account available scientific and technical data, particularly with reference to respective nitrogen contributions originating from agricultural and other sources, and regional environmental conditions.
For the purposes of regulation 10(5), 'land management and cultivation practices' includes cleaning out ditches and installing drainage or irrigation.

These Regulations apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank meeting the requirements of paragraph (1) if any requirement of a notice under regulation 7 is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.

A person served with a regulation 30 notice may appeal to the Welsh Ministers against the notice within 28 days beginning on the day after the date on which the notice is served, or such longer period as the Welsh Ministers allow.

The Agency must refuse an application for a derogation if it considers that granting the derogation would have an adverse effect on the integrity of a European site or European offshore marine site that has been subject to an appropriate assessment under regulation 63 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017.

In a case within regulation 5(3A), the only ground of appeal under regulation 6 is that the relevant holding (or any part of it) does not drain into water which the Secretary of State has identified as polluted or which has been similarly identified in Wales or Scotland.

Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser during the relevant period, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate (kg) required, being the optimum amount required by the crop less the amount of phosphate that will be supplied for crop uptake from any organic manure spread.

In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may, as an alternative to the Schedule 1 calculation method, use software approved by the Secretary of State, or, where the system only produces solid manure, sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.
"Relevant water abstraction" means the abstraction of water for use for human consumption.

The panel must base its decision on documents submitted by the appellant, documents submitted by the Agency, and such additional information from the appellant or the Agency as it considers necessary.

Subject to regulation 6, no person shall have custody or control of any crop being made into silage or any silage being stored unless it is kept in a silo in relation to which the requirements of Schedule 1 are satisfied or which is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 5.

An owner or occupier of a relevant holding who is sent a notice under regulation 5(3)(b) or 5(3A)(b) may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal against the proposals or designation referred to in the notice.
An occupier must keep a copy of any advice from a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme that is relied on for any purpose under these Regulations for five years.
