statements.statement_text: A notice under regulation 4B must include a written statement that the occupier will comply with the additional requirements set out in Schedule 1A.
Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure that the occupier intends will be sent off the holding.
Solid poultry manure that does not have bedding mixed into it and is stored on a temporary field site must be covered with an impermeable material.
Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b), the occupier must update the risk map within one month of the change, beginning with the day after the change.
In regulation 40A, 'relevant period' means the period of four years beginning with 1 January 2016 and each successive period of four years.
The maximum nitrogen application rate for brassica is 100 kg/hectare.
NRW must withdraw a regulation 30 notice, extend the period for compliance, or modify the requirements of the notice if so directed by the Welsh Ministers under regulation 31(5).
The records required by paragraph 17(1) and (2) must be made before 1 March 2024.
A temporary field site must not be within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well, or within 10 metres of surface water or a land drain (other than a sealed impermeable pipe).

Where a silo has a capacity of 1500 cubic metres or more, the capacity of the effluent tank shall be not less than 30 cubic metres plus 1 cubic metre for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity in excess of 1500 cubic metres.
A person using sampling and analysis to determine nitrogen content in organic manure must keep the original report from the laboratory.

Schedule 1 sets out the daily manure (in litres or, for poultry, kilograms), nitrogen and phosphate produced by each non-grazing livestock animal by category, for the purposes of Regulations 2(1), 7(3), 25(1) and (2), 26(1), 27(1) and (2) and 34(4) of UKSI 2015/668.
A person on whom a regulation 7 notice has been served must comply with the requirements of that notice.
In the Conservation of Habitats and Species (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, regulation 104, paragraph (1)(b) and the 'or' before it are omitted.
The base of a silo must be designed in accordance with BS 8007: 1987 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for design of concrete structures for retaining aqueous liquids).

After acting in reliance on regulation 13, the occupier must provide the FACTS adviser with soil analyses from representative autumn soil samples so that the adviser may take the analyses into account when advising for subsequent years.

required_context.locator: Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme (FACTS)

statements.statement_text: Where organic manure (other than livestock manure) is supplied by a manufacturer or other supplier, the nitrogen content and available nitrogen may alternatively be calculated by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.
An occupier who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must first undertake a field inspection to consider the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water.

A reference to 'polluted water' in these Regulations means water that is freshwater and contains a concentration of nitrates greater than 50 mg/l (or could do so if these Regulations were not to apply there).

Regulation 25 does not apply to a new holding until the latest date on which a closed period under regulation 20 begins in relation to that holding, regardless of whether an exception under regulation 20(4) or 21 applies.
The volume of manure produced by animals on a holding must be calculated in accordance with Schedule 1.

Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank may have a lesser capacity than the two-day maximum where the Agency agrees in writing that the lesser capacity is adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.
Where livestock manure has been spread on grass not on sandy soils on the holding between 15 October and the following 15 January, the grass must not be ploughed before the following 16 January.

Where an appeal has been made against a regulation 7 notice, the compliance period is extended (subject to any direction under paragraph (5)) so that it expires on the date the Secretary of State finally determines the appeal, or, if the appeal is withdrawn, on the date of withdrawal.
The offence provision in paragraph (3) does not apply to contraventions under regulations 24(1), 24(4), 25(1), 30(5) or 32.
The total nitrogen content of pig slurry is 3.6 kg per cubic metre, as specified in the standard table for calculating nitrogen in manure.
A land manager must ensure that organic manure is not stored on agricultural land within 10 metres of inland freshwaters or coastal waters.

The spreading plan must be in permanent form and must record, for each relevant field and area planted or intended to be planted, specified information including field reference, area, crop type, soil type, previous crop, soil nitrogen supply and method, anticipated planting month, anticipated yield (if arable), and optimum nitrogen amount.
The total nitrogen content of dirty water is 0.5 kg per cubic metre, as specified in the standard table for calculating nitrogen in manure.

If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under regulation 6(2)(b), the Secretary of State when acting under regulation 4(5) must treat the water concerned as water which should not be identified, or should not continue to be identified, as polluted.
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on land during the closed period.

Regulations 24(1) and 25(1) do not apply to a silo or slurry storage system which, where it was not used before 1 March 1991 for making silage or storing slurry, was constructed before that date for such use.
A slurry storage system must satisfy the requirements set out in Schedule 2, paragraph 1 of SSI 2003/531.

The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, using the figures in Schedule 1.
The first report under regulation 40 must be published before 31 March 2020.
On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to extend the period for compliance with any requirement of the regulation 7 notice.
The occupier must make a record describing the livestock housing and manure storage systems together with the volume of manure storage in place on the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.
A derogation holder must observe a closed period for ploughing grass as a condition of the derogation.

An area is designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone if it is an area of land that drains into polluted waters, contributes to the pollution of those waters, and is marked as such a zone on a relevant map.
A report published under regulation 16 must assess the extent to which the objectives of the regulatory provision referred to in paragraph (1)(a) are achieved.
In the Water Environment (Water Framework Directive) (England and Wales) Regulations 2017, Schedule 2 Part 2, paragraph 24 is substituted with new text as specified.
A reference to a slurry storage system in these Regulations includes a slurry storage tank together with any reception pit and any effluent tank used in connection with the tank.

Where a silo has retaining walls, the silo must not at any time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumptions made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.
The prohibition in paragraph (1) does not apply where the occupier has been granted a derogation.
An occupier who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.

The occupier must, during the relevant period, record within one week of ploughing grass on the holding the date of that ploughing, in addition to the requirements of regulation 41 (subsequent records).

Where the Agency grants an application in a case within paragraph (8) or decides not to revoke a derogation in a case within paragraph (9), it must refuse the next application made under regulation 36 by or on behalf of the occupier.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil to be kept in a new or improved store must give the Agency notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location, at least 14 days before construction work is to be begun.
In the case of grass, nitrogen must not be spread after 31 October, and a maximum of 40 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time.
In assessing the significant risk of nitrogen entering surface water, account must be taken of ground cover, the proximity to surface water, and weather conditions.

The period for compliance with a regulation 30 notice against which an appeal has been made is automatically extended so that it expires on the date on which the Welsh Ministers finally determine the appeal, or, if the appeal is withdrawn, the date on which it is withdrawn, subject to any direction under regulation 31(5).
The maximum nitrogen application rate for over-wintered salad onions is 40 kg/hectare.
The occupier of a holding must maintain a record of the total size of the holding calculated in accordance with regulation 4(3).
The occupier of a holding who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.
Part 2 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser on a crop growing in a greenhouse.
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulations 15 to 35 commits an offence.
The occupier may exceed the storage capacity limit where the three specified conditions are met.
Within one week of spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the area on which organic manure is spread.
A heap of solid manure forming a temporary field site must occupy as small a surface area as is practically required to support the mass of the heap and prevent it from collapse.

An exempt structure to which regulation 5(a) circumstances apply shall cease to be an exempt structure if any requirement of a notice under regulation 8(1) is not complied with within the period stated in the notice.
Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the occupier must record the month in which it is planned to do the spreading.

As part of the review under regulation 39, the Secretary of State must review the overall position of derogations granted under this regulation against the objective criterion of net rainfall in designated nitrate vulnerable zones.

Where any part of an effluent tank is installed below ground level, it shall be designed and constructed in accordance with BS 5502 (as referred to in paragraph 7(a)) so that, with proper maintenance, it is likely to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 for a period of at least 20 years.

The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank if that other tank is of equal or greater capacity, or if the tops of the tanks are at the same level.

The fertilisation account must record: the amount, type and characteristics of livestock manure sent off the holding; the nitrogen and phosphate content of that manure; the weight and nitrogen/phosphate content of all manufactured fertiliser stocks held, brought on to, and sent off the holding during the relevant period.
The factors to be considered under paragraph (3) include those specified in regulation 4(2).
Where the walls of a silo, its effluent tank, channels or pipes are made of earth, they shall be lined with an impermeable membrane.

In calculating the area of the holding for the purposes of ascertaining the amount of nitrogen to be spread, no account is taken of surface waters, any hardstanding, buildings, roads, or any woodland unless that woodland is used for grazing.

In calculating the area of the holding for the purposes of ascertaining the permitted nitrogen spread, no account is taken of surface waters, any hardstanding, buildings, roads, or any woodland unless that woodland is used for grazing.
A structure to which the circumstances at regulation 5(a) apply ceases to be an exempt structure if it is substantially enlarged.

The Agency must make recommendations to the Secretary of State as to which areas of land should be, or should continue to be, designated as nitrate vulnerable zones, by reference to the matters in regulation 4(5)(a) to (c), before 10th August 2016 and before 10th August of every fourth year thereafter.
The risk map must correspond with the agricultural area of the holding.

No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in a fuel storage tank or container which is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 5, or in an underground fuel storage tank or container.

Between the end of the closed period and the end of the following February: (a) the maximum amount of slurry that may be spread at any one time is 30 cubic metres per hectare; (b) the maximum amount of poultry manure that may be spread at any one time is 8 tonnes per hectare; (c) there must be at least three weeks between any spreading of slurry or poultry manure.
The occupier of a holding must, within one week of spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, record the date of spreading.

Having determined an appeal under regulation 38, the panel must as soon as reasonably practicable notify in writing the Agency, the appellant and the Secretary of State of its determination, and where it refuses the appeal, give the reasons for its refusal.
Before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, the occupier of a holding must record the amount required and the month in which it is planned to spread it.

In the case of any crop other than permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the soil assessment requirement before spreading any nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or intended to be planted.
The total amount of nitrogen which the occupier may spread on any given hectare must not exceed 700 kg if the grass is irrigated.
A person having custody or control of slurry must have a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 6, and the slurry must be stored in that system.
For the purposes of regulation 9, 'construction' includes substantial enlargement and reconstruction.
The Agency must refuse a derogation application if the occupier has been found in breach of the derogation conditions during the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in an underground fuel storage tank.

The risk map must show each field with its area in hectares, all surface waters, any boreholes/springs/wells on or within 50 metres of the holding boundary, areas with sandy or shallow soils, land with an incline greater than 12°, land within 10 metres of surface waters, land within 50 metres of a borehole/spring/well, land drains (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), sites suitable for temporary field heaps if that storage method is to be used, and (optionally) land with a low run-off risk.
Parts 3 to 8 of UKSI 2015/668 apply only in relation to holdings that are in nitrate vulnerable zones designated for the purposes of these Regulations.
After mixing the sub-samples, a representative sample of at least 2 kg must be sent for analysis.

Where a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on that pipe, each capable of stopping the flow of slurry, and each valve must be kept shut and locked when not in use.
On determining an appeal under regulation 9, the Scottish Ministers may direct SEPA to withdraw the notice.

Where the occupier of a holding introduces animals on to the holding for the first time, the occupier must, within one month of that introduction, calculate and record the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, using the figures given in Schedule 1.
A notice served under the relevant provision must inform the recipient of the effect in relation to the notice of regulation 9.
The fertilisation plan must be in permanent form.

For the purposes of regulation 25, land has a 'low run-off risk' if it has an average slope of less than 3 degrees, does not have land drains (other than a sealed impermeable pipe), and is at least 50 metres from a watercourse or conduit leading to a watercourse.

A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.
For solid manures, at least ten samples of 1 kg each must be taken, each from a different location in a heap, and each sample must be taken at least 0.5 metres from the surface of the heap.

An occupier of a holding who intends to spread nitrogen fertiliser must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season (the soil nitrogen supply).
On sandy or shallow soil, the closed period for spreading slurry or manure on grassland runs from 1st September to the following 31st December.

Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under regulation 41 and the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or attributable to neglect by, a director, manager, secretary, other similar officer, or person purporting to act in such a capacity, that individual is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

Where a body corporate is guilty of an offence under these Regulations, and that offence is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or attributable to neglect on the part of a person purporting to act as director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate, that person is also guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
The occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the type and amount of livestock manure.
The occupier must make a record of the expected number and category of livestock to be kept on the holding during the relevant period, using the categories in Tables 1 and 2 in Schedule 1.
The occupier, or any person on behalf of the occupier, must submit fertilisation accounts for the relevant period to NRW by 31 March 2025, and such accounts must be submitted by e-mail.
A person must not spread nitrogen fertiliser if the soil is waterlogged, flooded or snow covered.

The Agency may impose a fixed monetary penalty in relation to an offence under regulation 41, as if it were an offence specified in Schedule 5 to the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010.

A notice under regulation 4B must include a written statement that the occupier intends during the relevant period to apply to the holding a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure which exceeds 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
The occupier must, before spreading organic manure, record the area on which the organic manure will be spread.
In regulation 32, 'construction' includes substantial enlargement and reconstruction.

In the case of any crop other than those covered by preceding provisions, the occupier must comply with the duty under paragraph (1) before spreading any nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or intended to be planted.

A person served with a regulation 7 notice may appeal to the Secretary of State against the notice within 28 days beginning on the day after the date on which the notice is served, or such longer period as the Secretary of State allows.

Before determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State must, if requested by the appellant or the Agency, afford them an opportunity to appear before and be heard by a person appointed by the Secretary of State for that purpose.
An expression used in regulation 42(1) and in the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Order has the same meaning in that paragraph as it has in that Order.
The Secretary of State must from time to time carry out a review of the regulatory provision contained in these Regulations.

A person served with a regulation 7 notice may appeal to the Secretary of State against the notice within 28 days beginning on the day after the date on which the notice is served, or such longer period as the Secretary of State allows.
Throughout the year concerned, the occupier must not bring organic manure on to the holding.

A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of any relevant substance to be kept or stored on a farm in a silo, slurry storage system, or fuel storage area constructed, substantially enlarged, or substantially reconstructed on or after 29 December 2003 must serve notice on SEPA specifying the type of structure to be used and its location at least 28 days before it is to be used for that purpose.
The surface area of a temporary field site must be as small as reasonably practicable to minimise the leaching effect of rainfall.

A person is not entitled to rely on the bulk bagged silage exemption conferred by regulation 6(1) unless that person stores any bags in which silage is being made or stored at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.
Land comes within regulation 17(3) if it is notified as a site of special scientific interest under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage or slurry to be kept in a new or improved store must give NRW notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location at least 14 days before work constructing the new or improved store is to be begun.

The enhanced nutrient management plan must record the amount of nitrogen (kg) likely to be available for crop uptake from any organic manure intended to be spread in the growing season during the relevant period, and the amount of phosphate (kg) likely to be supplied to meet crop requirements from any organic manure spread or intended to be spread during the relevant period, calculated in accordance with tables 1 and 2 of Schedule 1, sampling and analysis under Part 2 of Schedule 3, or technical analyses provided by the supplier.

An exempt structure to which regulation 5(a) circumstances apply shall cease to be an exempt structure if it is substantially reconstructed, unless in SEPA's opinion (notified in writing) the risks of pollution will be reduced by such works.
Checking spreading equipment for leaks and correct calibration is an example of a reasonable precaution for the purposes of compliance with regulation 4(3).
In the case of grass, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
Where a silo has a capacity of less than 1,500 cubic metres, the capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 20 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity.
Crop rotation on the holding must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen, except for grass with less than 50% clover.

The fertilisation account must record the total agricultural area of the holding in hectares and the area covered by specified crops (winter wheat, spring wheat, winter barley, spring barley, winter oilseed rape, sugar beet, potatoes, forage maize, grass, and other crops).
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulation 37(3) commits an offence.

Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record, for the previous storage period referred to in regulation 29, the number and category of animals in a building or on a hardstanding during that storage period.
For each area planted or intended to be planted, the nutrient management plan must record the previous crop, and where the previous crop was grass, whether it was managed by cutting or grazing.
The occupier must retain written confirmation that the organic manure complies with the certified compost definition in sub-paragraph (b).
An occupier must record how any grassland was managed in the previous calendar year, before 30 April each year.
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulations 7, 8, 10 to 13, 15 to 35, or regulation 37(3) commits an offence.
The base of a slurry storage tank must be impermeable.

In calculating the area of a holding for the purpose of ascertaining the permitted nitrogen spread, no account is to be taken of: (a) any surface waters, hardstanding, buildings, roads or woodland (unless the woodland is used for grazing); or (b) any land covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the year concerned.

The 'total amount of nitrogen' means the total of (a) the amount of nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser, and (b) the amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure in the growing season in which it is spread, calculated in accordance with regulation 14.

Where a silo has retaining walls, the silo must at no time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumption made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.

When planning to avoid a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution, a land manager must take into account specified risk factors including: slope of the land (in particular if greater than 12 degrees), ground cover, proximity to inland freshwaters, coastal waters, wetlands, or a spring, well or borehole, soil type and condition, and the presence and condition of any agricultural land drains.

Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be spread within 10 metres of surface water if: it is spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as species-rich semi-natural grassland that is notified as SSSI or subject to an agri-environmental commitment; it is spread between 1 June and 31 October; it is not spread directly onto surface water; and the total annual amount does not exceed 12.5 tonnes per hectare.
For the purposes of paragraph (6)(c), the panel may request the appellant or the Agency to provide additional information.

A report under regulation 40(2)(a) must include an assessment of whether the objectives of these Regulations remain appropriate and, in so far as they do, the extent to which they could be achieved in a less burdensome way.
A record required under paragraph 14 must be made by 1st March for the calendar year concerned.
A land manager must ensure that each application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to agricultural land is planned so that it does not exceed the needs of the soil and crop on that land.

The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and of any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of BS 5502: Part 50: 1993.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must on each occasion calculate the amount of nitrogen that is likely to be available from that manure for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.
The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) Regulations 2013 are revoked.

If the occupier is found in breach of the derogation conditions after the date of the application but before it has been determined (and before the calendar year to which the application relates), the Agency may, taking into account the seriousness of the breach, grant or refuse the application.

For the period beginning 1 December 2016 and ending on the day the Secretary of State next revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means the map marked 'Nitrate Vulnerable Zones (England) 2017 to 2020' published on 1 December 2016 on the Agency's website.
In proceedings for an offence under regulation 11(1), it is a defence for a person to show that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

Where any grass on the holding is ploughed during the relevant period, the land must be sown with a crop with high nitrogen demand within four weeks beginning with the day after the date of ploughing grass.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that the total amount of nitrogen spread on a crop or group of crops specified in the table in regulation 12(4) does not exceed the figure specified in the second column of that table in any twelve-month period, adjusted as specified in the notes and multiplied by the total area in hectares of the crop or group sown on the holding.

The occupier of a holding who has submitted an undertaking to the organic control system under Article 27 of Council Regulation (EC) 834/2007 may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on winter oilseed rape, asparagus, brassica, grass, over-wintered salad onions, parsley or bulb onions, notwithstanding regulation 20.

Facilities used for the temporary storage of slurry before transfer to a slurry storage tank must have adequate capacity to store the maximum quantity of slurry likely to be produced on the premises in any two-day period (disregarding slurry transferred directly into a slurry storage tank).

For organic manure other than livestock manure, the nitrogen content and available nitrogen must be calculated either by reference to values given in the Fertiliser Manual or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.

The occupier must establish the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure for the purposes of regulation 8 by either using the table in Part 1 of Schedule 3 or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3.

In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry where the system of keeping livestock only produces solid manure, the occupier may use sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 3 as an alternative method.
Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in paragraph 7(1), the occupier must update the risk map within one month of the change.
No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in drums within a storage area satisfying the requirements of Schedule 3.
The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.
A person having custody or control of slurry must store it only in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2.
A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth shall not be filled to a level which allows less than 750 millimetres of freeboard.
"Orchard land" means land on which any fruit listed in Schedule 2 is grown.

Where the occupier of a qualifying grassland holding intends during the relevant period to apply a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares, the occupier must submit a notice to NRW in accordance with regulation 4B.

A person who contravenes regulation 4(1) of the Regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum, or on conviction on indictment to a fine.
The records required under paragraph 18(1) must be made by 1 March 2024.

Where a person uses equipment to spread slurry by broadcasting and the equipment has a trajectory of 4 metres or more from the ground, the equipment must be able to achieve a maximum slurry application rate of 1 mm per hour when operating continuously.
These Regulations apply in relation to Wales.
In regulation 32, 'construction' includes substantial enlargement and reconstruction.
Regulation 2 shall not apply where a person makes bulk bagged silage on a farm in bags that are kept sealed to prevent the escape of silage effluent.
The maximum nitrogen application rate for grass is 80 kg/hectare.
Where a change in circumstances affects a matter referred to in paragraph (1), the occupier must update the risk map within three months of the change.
A decision of the panel is to be made by simple majority.
A reference to 'polluted water' in these Regulations also means water that is eutrophic, or may in the near future become eutrophic if these Regulations were not to apply there.
Any person spreading nitrogen fertiliser must do so in as accurate a manner as possible.
A person who contravenes regulation 32 is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale.
For pig slurry, the available nitrogen for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread is 50% (applicable on and after 1st January 2014).

'Relevant holding' means land and any associated buildings at the disposal of the occupier which are used for growing crops in soil or rearing livestock for agricultural purposes, and which are wholly or partly in an area which the Secretary of State has proposed should be, or has designated as, a nitrate vulnerable zone.
On conviction on indictment for an offence under regulation 11, a person is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or a fine, or both.

In the case of brassica, an additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the applicable closed period under regulation 20, up to the date of harvest, but not so as to exceed the limit imposed by paragraph (2).
A silo must comply with the provisions of Schedule 5 in order to satisfy the requirement imposed in relation to it.
On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to modify any of the requirements of the regulation 7 notice.
These Regulations come into force on 1 April 2021.
Where livestock manure has been spread on grass on sandy soils on the holding between 1 September and 31 December, the grass must not be ploughed before the following 16 January.
SEPA may at any time modify any requirement of a notice served under regulation 8, provided the person on whom the notice is served consents.
On determining an appeal under regulation 31, the Welsh Ministers may direct NRW to modify any of the requirements of the regulation 30 notice.

When planning the application of agricultural diffuse pollution sources, the land manager must ensure that the slope of the land (in particular if greater than 12 degrees) is taken into account as a factor indicating significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution.
For the purposes of paragraph (3), 'officer' means a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body.

Any organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) spread on land within 50 metres of surface water that slopes such that there may be run-off to that water must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest.
For other livestock manure (not cattle slurry, pig slurry, or poultry manure), 10% of the total nitrogen is assumed to be available for crop uptake in the growing season in which it is spread.

Where a silo has retaining walls, the silo must at no time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumptions made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.

A notice under regulation 5(3)(b) or 5(3A)(b) must contain a reference to the page on the Agency's or Secretary of State's website on which can be found the Secretary of State's proposals or, where the designation has already been revised or added to, the designation.
Where fuel from a tank is delivered through a permanently attached flexible pipe, the pipe must be fitted with a tap or valve at its end that closes automatically when not in use.

Where the occupier of a holding introduces animals on to the holding for the first time, the occupier must, within one month of that introduction, calculate and record the current storage capacity of the holding.

For the purposes of regulation 8, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure is to be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14; and the land on the holding to which the 250kg limit applies does not include any land covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the period concerned.

The occupier may rely on the result of previous phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type for the purposes of the four-yearly obligation, provided the sampling and analysis was carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation.

"Certified compost" means green compost or green/food compost in relation to which the supplier confirms in writing that it meets the standards set out in PAS 100:2011 on composted materials dated January 2011 and contains no livestock manure.
The Nitrate Pollution Prevention (Wales) (Amendment) Regulations 2019 are revoked.
The results of soil sampling and analysis must include the pH of the soil and the levels of nitrogen, phosphorous, magnesium and potassium present.
A person may spread fertiliser during the closed period on a crop not specified in the table in paragraph (5) if the spreading is in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser.

statements.statement_text: No part of a fuel storage area or its enclosing bund may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that fuel oil could enter if it were to escape.
If the amount of storage capacity changes, the occupier must record the change within one week.
The standard total nitrogen content of pig slurry is 3.6 kg per cubic metre for the purposes of calculating nitrogen in organic manure under Regulations 9, 36 and 37.

Where a person uses equipment to spread slurry by broadcasting and the equipment has a trajectory of 4 metres or more from the ground, the equipment must be able to achieve a maximum slurry application rate of 1 mm per hour when operating continuously.
No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or any associated pipes shall be situated within 10 metres of any inland or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the current storage capacity of the holding.

The enhanced nutrient management plan must record the amount of manufactured nitrogen fertiliser (kg) required (being the optimum nitrogen required by the crop less the nitrogen available from organic manure spread during the relevant period) and the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser (kg) required (being the optimum phosphate required by the crop less the phosphate supplied from organic manure spread for fertilising the crop during the relevant period).
These Regulations come into force on 1 April 2021.
When carrying out a review under paragraph (2), the Welsh Ministers must take into account regional environmental conditions.

The two-valve requirement does not apply to a slurry storage tank that drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank if that other tank is of equal or greater capacity, or if the tops of the tanks are at the same level.

Regulation 2 shall not apply where a person makes bulk bagged silage on a farm in bags that are stored on a firm level surface and incorporate a facility designed to enable the safe removal of excess effluent when present.

Spreading slurry/manure during the closed periods on crops not listed in Schedule 4 is permitted where it is carried out on the basis of written advice from a person who is a member of the Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme.

required_context.locator: Fertiliser Advisers Certification and Training Scheme (FACTS)

statements.statement_text: Spreading organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil is permitted between 1 August and 15 September inclusive, provided that the crop is sown on or before 15 September.
A silo must comply with the provisions of Schedule 5 in order to satisfy the requirement imposed in relation to it.
A notice under regulation 4B must include the address of the qualifying grassland holding.

For agricultural land to which paragraph (2) does not apply, the land manager must ensure that any factors which mean there would be a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution are taken into account when deciding where to locate a livestock feeder.
The risk map for the holding must be completed by 1st March in the calendar year to which it relates.

If the First-tier Tribunal upholds an appeal under paragraph (2)(a), the Secretary of State, when acting under regulation 4(5), must treat the relevant holding (or the part of it in respect of which the appeal was upheld) as not draining into the water concerned.

The period for compliance with a regulation 7 notice against which an appeal has been made is automatically extended so that it expires on the date on which the Secretary of State finally determines the appeal, or, if the appeal is withdrawn, on the date of withdrawal, subject to any direction under regulation 8(5).
Any person spreading slurry must use spreading equipment with a low spreading trajectory, that is, below 4 metres from the ground.

Regulation 8 does not apply where: (a) the requirements in regulation 8(7) are met (at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass; total nitrogen in organic manure applied does not exceed 100kg multiplied by the holding's area in hectares; total nitrogen from manufactured nitrogen fertiliser does not exceed 90kg multiplied by the holding's area in hectares; and the occupier does not bring organic manure onto the holding throughout the year concerned); and (b) the occupier makes a record demonstrating that those requirements are met.

Following any subsequent review under regulation 4(5), 'relevant map' means a map published on the Agency's website that is marked 'This map identifies those areas of England designated by the Secretary of State as a Nitrate Vulnerable Zone for the purposes of the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2015 (England).' and specifies the period to which it relates.

A person is not entitled to rely on the exemption conferred by paragraph (1) unless that person stores any bags in which silage is being made or stored at a place at least 10 metres from any inland or coastal waters.

The base and walls of a slurry storage tank and any reception pit must be capable of withstanding characteristic loads calculated on the assumptions and in the manner indicated by paragraph 5 of the Code of Practice.

Regulation 24 (closed period for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser) does not apply in relation to a new holding until 31st July in the third calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include the new holding.

A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain: (a) details of any steps taken to promote good agricultural practice; (b) the map published under regulation 3(2) accompanied by a statement detailing the nature of and reasons for any revisions to the designated nitrate vulnerable zone since the end of the previous reporting period; (c) a summary of the monitoring results obtained by the Agency under regulation 4; and (d) a summary of the most recent review conducted under regulation 39.

Enhanced nutrient management requirements apply to the occupier of a qualifying grassland holding who intends, during the relevant period, to apply to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) a total amount of nitrogen in grazing livestock manure exceeding 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
Where all fuel oil in the storage area is contained in one tank, the bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of that tank.

The base of a silo must be constructed using appropriate hot-rolled asphalt in accordance with BS 5502: Part 21: 1990 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for selection and use of construction materials), as an alternative to the BS 8007: 1987 design standard.

Any organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) applied to land within 50 metres of surface water that slopes such that there may be run-off to that water must be incorporated as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest.
On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to withdraw the regulation 7 notice.
A person spreading nitrogen fertiliser must do so in as accurate a manner as possible.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the area on which the manure is to be spread.

The requirement in paragraph (1) shall not apply to slurry while it is stored temporarily in a tanker with a capacity not exceeding 18,000 litres which is used for transporting slurry on roads or about a farm.

The Agency must refuse a derogation application if it considers that granting the derogation would have an adverse effect on the integrity of a European site or European offshore marine site that has been subject to an appropriate assessment under regulation 63 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017.
Regulation 8 does not apply where the requirements in paragraph (7) are met and the occupier makes a record demonstrating that those requirements are met.

Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must have adequate provision for the drainage of slurry from the collection channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.

Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the occupier must record the amount required, being the optimum amount of phosphate required by the crop less the amount of phosphate that will be supplied for crop uptake from any organic manure spread.
For oilseed rape (winter), the maximum nitrogen application rate during the closed period is 30 kg/hectare.
In proceedings for an offence under regulation 11(1), it is a defence for a person to show that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

The requirement to include information on land with a low run-off risk in the risk map does not apply to an occupier who does not intend to spread manure on such land during the storage period referred to in regulation 25.

In relation to organic manure (other than livestock manure) supplied by a manufacturer or other supplier, the nitrogen content and available nitrogen must be calculated by reference to the supplier's technical analyses or, where unavailable, the values in the Fertiliser Manual, or by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.

The base and walls of the slurry storage tank, any effluent tank, channels and reception pit, and the walls of any pipes must be protected against corrosion in accordance with paragraph 7.2 of BS 5502 (Part 50: 1993).
Any reference in regulation 6(2) to a requirement of a notice means that requirement as modified if it has been modified under regulation 7(5).
Any person spreading slurry must use spreading equipment with a low spreading trajectory, that is, below 4 metres from the ground.
Any person spreading nitrogen fertiliser must do so in as accurate a manner as possible.

The occupier of a holding who brings livestock manure onto a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the type and amount of livestock manure, the date on which it was brought onto the holding, the nitrogen content (if known), and the name and address of the supplier.
The period for compliance stated in a notice is 28 days or such longer period as is reasonable in the circumstances.

If a slurry storage tank, effluent tank, or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, there must be two valves in series on the pipe, with each valve separated from the other by a minimum distance of 1 metre.
Slurry storage systems must comply with the requirements set out in Schedule 2.
The risk map for the holding must correspond with the agricultural area of the holding.
No person shall have custody or control of fuel oil on a farm unless it is stored in a fuel storage tank or container within a storage area satisfying the requirements of Schedule 3.

For the purposes of regulation 28, nitrogen content must be ascertained either by using the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 2, or by sampling and analysis as set out in Part 2 of that Schedule.

When carrying out the review under paragraph (1)(a), the Secretary of State must take into account available scientific and technical data, particularly with reference to respective nitrogen contributions originating from agricultural or other sources.

The restrictions in regulation 40(1) and (2) do not apply to the occupier of a holding in any calendar year in which 80% of the agricultural area of the holding is sown with grass, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure applied (whether directly by animal or by spreading) is no more than 100 kg per hectare, the total amount of nitrogen in manufactured nitrogen fertiliser applied is no more than 90 kg per hectare, and the occupier does not bring any organic manure onto the holding.
For the purposes of regulation 41(3), 'director', in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, means a member of the body.
A person (P) may not rely on a defence under paragraph (1) involving a third party allegation unless P has served a notice in accordance with paragraph (3) or obtained the leave of the court.

In assessing whether it was reasonable for P to rely on information supplied by another person, particular regard must be had to the steps P took, and those which might reasonably have been taken, for the purpose of verifying the information.
A temporary field site must not be in a field liable to flooding or becoming waterlogged.
For the purposes of regulation 10(5), 'land management and cultivation practices' includes creating farm tracks on, or gateways to, the land.

NRW may serve a regulation 30 notice on a person who has custody or control of silage or slurry, or is responsible for a silo or slurry storage system, requiring that person to carry out works or take precautions or other steps specified in the notice, where these Regulations apply.

A person served with a notice under regulation 8 may appeal to the Scottish Ministers against that notice within 28 days beginning with the day on which the notice is served, or within such longer period as the Scottish Ministers may allow.
The reference to the agricultural area in paragraph (1) does not include any land which is covered by a greenhouse.

If the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must ascertain it as soon as reasonably practicable after arrival and record it within one week of ascertaining it.
The total amount of nitrogen which the occupier may spread on any given hectare must not exceed 700 kg if the grass is irrigated, or 500 kg if the grass is not irrigated.
The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any 12 month period, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure spread on any given hectare on the holding does not exceed 250 kg.

The total amount of nitrogen in the form of green compost or green/food compost spread on any given hectare of land on the holding must not exceed 500 kg in any two-year period, whether spread as mulch or incorporated into the soil.
A person who has custody or control of fuel oil on a farm must ensure that it is stored in drums within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.
Land has a 'low run-off risk' for the purposes of regulation 25 if it does not have land drains (other than a sealed impermeable pipe).
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading organic manure, the total phosphorus content.
The base of the silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
A notice served under the relevant provision must state the period within which any requirement specified in the notice is to be complied with.
Before spreading organic manure during the relevant period, the occupier must record the total phosphate content (kg) of the organic manure.

A water supply source is a protected water supply source for the purposes of regulation 24(1)(c)(ii) if the silage was made elsewhere and the person making or storing the silage was aware of the source's location before the silage was stored on the land in question.
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on grassland during the closed period, which begins on 15 September and ends on the following 15 January.
Any person required to make a record under WSI 2021/77 must keep that record for five years.

The risk map may optionally show land that has a low run-off risk; this is optional for an occupier who does not intend to spread manure on low run-off risk land during the storage period in accordance with regulation 29.
An occupier who introduces animals onto a holding for the first time must comply with the requirements of paragraph (1) within one month of the introduction of the animals.

Before 30 April each year, the occupier of a holding with livestock must record the number of animals on the holding during the previous calendar year and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1.
Where a silo has a capacity of less than 1500 cubic metres, the capacity of the effluent tank shall be not less than 3 cubic metres for each 150 cubic metres or part thereof of silo capacity.
These Regulations may be cited as the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010.

When planning an application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to cultivated agricultural land under regulation 4(1)(a), a land manager must ensure that the results of soil sampling and analysis are taken into account.

On determining an appeal under regulation 8, the Secretary of State may direct the Agency to withdraw the regulation 7 notice, modify any of its requirements, extend the period for compliance with any requirement, or dismiss the appeal.

In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry where the system of keeping livestock only produces solid manure, the occupier may use sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2 as an alternative method to that referred to in paragraph (2).
Having carried out a review under paragraph (1), the Secretary of State must publish the report.
Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought onto a holding is not known, the occupier must ascertain it as soon as reasonably practicable after arrival.
A notice must inform the person of the effect of regulation 8.

The provisions of the Environmental Civil Sanctions (England) Order 2010 relating to the sanctions referred to in regulation 42(1) apply as if they were provisions of the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010.

A reference to an EU Directive in these Regulations is to be read as if any reference in that Directive to one or more member States in a provision imposing an obligation on, or conferring a discretion on, a member State or member States were a reference to the authority which, immediately before exit day, was responsible for the United Kingdom's compliance with that obligation, or able to exercise that discretion, in respect of England.
A derogation holder must keep records of nitrogen and phosphate produced by animals as a condition of the derogation.
A notice must specify or describe the works, precautions or other steps that the person is required to carry out or take.
Before 30 April each year an occupier must record how any grassland was managed in the previous calendar year.
A person must not spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.

In the case of orchard land, the total amount of nitrogen in the form of green compost or green/food compost spread on any given hectare must not exceed 1,000 kg in any four-year period, provided it is spread as mulch.
The occupier must make a record of the calculations and how the final figures were arrived at, and an occupier who used software approved by the Welsh Ministers must keep a printout of the result.
The occupier of a holding must ensure that in any twelve-month period, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure spread on any given hectare of land on the holding does not exceed 250 kg.

The slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.
In order to comply with the review duty under regulation 39(1), the Secretary of State must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of the restrictions.
The daily manure, nitrogen and phosphate production figures for non-grazing livestock set out in Table 2 of Schedule 1 apply for the purposes of Regulations 3, 4, 29, 34 and 36.
Where a silo has a capacity of less than 1,500 cubic metres, the capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 20 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity.

An enforcement notice under regulation 8 must specify or describe the required works, precautions or other steps, state the period for compliance, and inform the recipient of the effect of regulation 9 in relation to the notice.

When planning an application of organic manure or manufactured fertiliser to cultivated agricultural land under regulation 4(1)(a), a land manager must ensure that the results of soil sampling and analysis are taken into account.
The maximum nitrogen application rate for winter oilseed rape is 30 kg/hectare.
Having carried out consultation under this regulation, the Secretary of State must inform the public about the decisions taken and the reasons for them.

For agricultural land to which the closed period prohibition does not apply, the land manager must ensure that any factors which mean there would be a significant risk of agricultural diffuse pollution are taken into account when deciding where to store organic manure.
These Regulations do not apply to a silo, slurry storage system or fuel storage tank which, before 1st March 1991, was being used for the purpose of making silage, storing slurry or storing fuel oil.
A slurry storage tank not having walls made of earth must have at least 300 mm of freeboard.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied from the organic manure intended to be spread for the purpose of fertilising the crop in the growing season in which it is spread.
The occupier must keep a record of the application and determination.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the date on which it was sent off the holding and the nitrogen content.
A person guilty of an offence under regulation 11 is liable, on summary conviction or on conviction on indictment, to a fine.
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of regulations 7 and 8 commits an offence.

In determining adequate storage capacity, account must be taken of the need to provide at least 750 millimetres of freeboard in the case of a tank with walls made of earth, and at least 300 millimetres of freeboard in all other cases.
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week, record the date it is sent off the holding and the nitrogen content.
In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may use software approved by the Secretary of State as an alternative method to that referred to in paragraph (2).
The Agency must make provision for a relevant map to be obtainable by persons without access to the internet.

Subject to paragraph 9, a silo, its effluent tank and channels and any pipes shall be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 5 and, if applicable, paragraph 7(a) for a period of at least 20 years.
No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
The base of the silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
The occupier of a holding with livestock must also record the temporary field sites used for free-standing heaps as referred to in regulation 23 and the dates of use.

The accounts must record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure produced by animals on the holding (by reference to Schedule 1), and the amount, type, characteristics, nitrogen and phosphate content of livestock manure brought onto or sent off the holding (calculated in accordance with paragraph 14(2)).

No person may spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water, except where precision spreading equipment is used, in which case no person may spread organic manure within 6 metres of surface water.
A person who fails to comply with the requirements of any of regulations 3 to 10 commits an offence.
The references in regulation 34(1) and (3) to 'the old regulations' are references to the Nitrate Pollution Prevention Regulations 2008.
The results of soil sampling and analysis must be no more than 5 years old at the time of the application.
These Regulations apply to agricultural land in England.

For the purposes of regulation 11(3), 'officer' means a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body, or a person purporting to act in any such capacity; and where a body corporate's affairs are managed by its members, regulation 11(3) applies to the acts and defaults of a member in connection with the member's management functions as it applies to an officer.
The occupier of a holding may apply to the Agency for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area of the holding (excluding land covered by a greenhouse) is sown with grass.

A person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil during the period beginning 1st August and ending the following 15th September, notwithstanding the prohibition in paragraph (2)(b), provided the next crop sown on the land is sown on or before 15th September.
In regulation 26, 'storage period' has the meaning given in regulation 25(7).

The occupier of a holding who has submitted an undertaking to the organic control system under Article 27 of Council Regulation (EC) 834/2007 may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on any other crop, provided this is done in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser, notwithstanding regulation 20.
